summary: xē'suelen nyahyan, hello everyone,
body_html:
xē'suelen nyahyan, hello everyone,

Last week, Alpha 4.10.3 opened to all waves in the PTU as we continued preparing for its upcoming release. As Vanduul attacks escalate across Nyx, the new InterSec Defense Solutions missions will put your combat skills to the test! We want to extend a huge thank you to everyone who jumped into the PTU over the weekend to help our teams test the latest update. We’re now reviewing the data and your reports as we work through the final improvements ahead of release. If you haven’t already, check out the latest PTU Patch Notes and share your thoughts in the dedicated feedback threads for Vanduul Incursion and the new Skarnov Rifle.

Following our recent announcement about updates to Pledge Gifting and Game Access, we also published a Pledge Gifting FAQ. These changes took effect on October 30, and we’ve gathered answers to some of your most frequently asked questions, along with additional clarification to help you better understand what’s changed and how it may affect your account.

Subscribers also received the October 2026 issue of Jump Point, taking you behind the scenes of RSI’s latest additions to the 'verse: the Constellation Mk V Centaurus and its smaller companion, the Skylark. If you're a Subscriber, grab your copy from the Subscriber section of your account.

Now let's see what's going on this week:

On Tuesday, Subscribers can look forward to the November Subscriber Comm-Link and Newsletter, bringing the latest exclusive flairs for the month ahead.

On Wednesday, the October 2026 PU Monthly Report will offer a look at what our teams have been working on over the past month, from gameplay and technology, to ships, art, and more. We’ll also publish a Roadmap Update and a Roadmap Roundup as we continue charting the course for upcoming releases.

Finally, on Friday, the latest RSI Weekly Newsletter also lands in your inbox. If you're not subscribed yet, you can sign up at any time through your account settings.

And looking a little further ahead, not this weekend, but the next, members of our team will be heading to Barcelona, Spain, for a Bar Citizen on Saturday, November 14! This will be the final stop on our Bar Citizen World Tour 2026, and we can't wait to wrap up an incredible year of community gatherings with you there!

a.thl’ē’kol, see you soon.

title: This Week in Star Citizen
summary: Happy Monday, everyone!
body_html:
Happy Monday, everyone!

Last week, the spooky season arrived with Day of the Vara, bringing the pumpkin decorating contest, the Arena Commander Festival Kill Collector FPS mode, and other fearsome finds for those brave enough to take part. We also released the latest Roadmap Update and Roundup, giving you a look at what’s ahead.

And for a closer look at the technology behind the work, the second episode of 10 From the Community is here, putting our Technical Directors in the spotlight to answer your questions about NPC behavior, social features, UI, ground vehicles, bug fixes, and more. We’re also gathering questions for a future FPS gameplay episode, so head to the Spectrum thread to submit yours and vote for the ones you’d most like to see answered.

Meanwhile, Alpha 4.10.3 landed on the PTU for Wave 1 testing, introducing a new Vanduul Incursion mission line to the Nyx System, a new energy rifle, along with a range of other additions and fixes. Thank you to everyone who’s jumped in to test, and for everyone still waiting, more waves will open up soon.

Now, let's see what's going on this week:

Later this week, we plan to release a Behind the Scenes video of the Squadron 42 October Event, giving you a peek behind the curtain at how things went.

This Friday, watch your inbox for the latest RSI Weekly Newsletter. Subscribers can also look forward to the October issue of Jump Point magazine.

And if racing is more your speed, the filthiest race in the ‘verse, the Daymar Rally, returns on January 23, 2027! Sign-ups are now open. Over 510 KM of unforgiving terrain awaits across three divisions. Gather your crew and see if you’ve got what it takes to conquer one legendary race across Daymar.

Cheers,

title: Roadmap Roundup - October 21, 2026
summary: Roadmap Roundup Hello everyone!
body_html:
Roadmap Roundup Hello everyone!

Every two weeks, we accompany the Roadmap update with a brief explanatory note to give you insight into the decision-making that led to any changes. This is part of an effort to make our communications more transparent, more specific, and more insightful for all of you who help to make Star Citizen and Squadron 42 possible.

Just a reminder: The 1.0 column showcases features and content planned for inclusion in or before Star Citizen 1.0. This means you may not have to wait for the 1.0 release to experience them. As features/content in the 1.0 column become ready, they will migrate left into a point patch column for release.

Be sure to check back every two weeks for the latest updates.

With that, let’s dive into this week’s Roadmap Roundup!

-CIG Community Team

Notable Changes: October 21, 2026

Release View

Alpha 4.10

Character Customization Update (Brows)

Implementing three new eyebrow styles and updating six existing options to bring them up to the current visual quality standard.

This card has been set to Released - Alpha 4.10.2

Intersec Defence Solutions Mission Pack

Implementing an expansion of Intersec Defence Solutions' contracts in Nyx, introducing new missions and gameplay opportunities centered on fighting the growing Vanduul threat, alongside new blueprints for players to earn.

This card has been added and set to Committed.

Join the discussion on Spectrum.

title: This Week in Star Citizen
summary: Happy Monday, everyone!
body_html:
Happy Monday, everyone!

There’s something about October that makes every strange noise aboard your ship a little more suspicious. That rattle in the cargo hold? Probably nothing. The lights flickering in the cockpit? Just a loose connection. Er, or a bug. Your co-pilot insisting they saw something move behind you? Okay, maybe it’s time to land.

We’ll leave the investigating to you. In the meantime, here’s what last week left behind.

The dead-stylish October Monthly Bundle crept out last Tuesday with a weathered black and gold finish and ethereal geometric etchings.

RSI Discovery Month is alive and kicking, and there’s still time to visit the RSI installations across Stanton. Take on Defense, Transport, and Collection missions and keep an eye on your mobiGlas as the rewards pile up. Everything you unlock, from ship paints and flight blades to armor, weapons, and tools, is yours to keep for good, no curse attached. Plus, completing the Constellation Rental Offer mission earns five days of access to the Constellation Mk V Centaurus. If you’d like a look at what’s waiting inside before you board, Behind the Ships and the Q&A have you covered.

The Twitch Drops are still lurking, too. Until October 27, watch any Drops-enabled Star Citizen stream for a total of four hours to unlock the Phoenix Insignia Display for free.

Don’t look behind you. Look ahead at what’s coming this week:

On Wednesday, we officially welcome the spooky season as the Day of the Vara festivities kick off, including a creepy contest, petrifying prizes, and other fearsome finds.

You’ll also see the latest Roadmap Update and its accompanying Roundup stumbling in behind them.

Friday brings our second episode of 10 From the Community, this time focusing on technology, with our Technical Directors stepping into the light. We’re also collecting questions for the next episode, all about FPS gameplay. Head to the Spectrum thread to submit yours and upvote the ones you’d most like to see answered!

The weekly RSI Newsletter also haunts your inbox that day, and if you’re not subscribed yet, you can sign up at any time through your account settings.

Whatever your plans this spooky season, we hope you’re getting into the spirit!

Fly low, fly fast, and keep the lights on...

title: Q&A: RSI Constellation Mk V Centaurus
summary: Q&A
body_html:
Q&A

Constellation Mk V Centaurus

by RSI

For generations, the Constellation has been part of life out there in our 'verse; a place for crews to work together, discover the extraordinary, and make a home among the stars. Through every era of space travel, it has helped people find their place and purpose. Now, RSI is honoring the Constellation’s inspiring legacy by introducing the Mk V for all the stories still to come.

We asked the Vehicle and Gameplay teams a few questions about this new generation of the Constellation series. Here are the answers, straight from the devs themselves.

Q&A:

Constellation Mk V

Centaurus

For generations, the Constellation has been part of life out there in our 'verse; a place for crews to work together, discover the extraordinary, and make a home among the stars. Through every era of space travel, it has helped people find their place and purpose. Now, RSI is honoring the Constellation’s inspiring legacy by introducing the Mk V for all the stories still to come.

We asked the Vehicle and Gameplay teams a few questions about this new generation of the Constellation series. Here are the answers, straight from the devs themselves.

Q&A

Constellation Mk V Centaurus

by RSI

For generations, the Constellation has been part of life out there in our 'verse; a place for crews to work together, discover the extraordinary, and make a home among the stars. Through every era of space travel, it has helped people find their place and purpose. Now, RSI is honoring the Constellation’s inspiring legacy by introducing the Mk V for all the stories still to come.

We asked the Vehicle and Gameplay teams a few questions about this new generation of the Constellation series. Here are the answers, straight from the devs themselves.

The Constellation series is one of the most recognizable ship lines in the 'verse. What sets the Mk V apart for players who are familiar with the Mk IV series? The Constellation Mk V takes fan-favorite elements of the Mk IV and brings them in line with modern RSI style and design. Players will find increased cargo capacity, allowing for a wider range of payloads, including some of our largest current ground vehicles. The ship itself has grown in all dimensions to accommodate this and has received other quality-of-life changes, such as access to internal missile restocking, internal component placement, and access as well as better habitation and accommodation spaces to allow the crew space to relax.

The size of the Constellation Mk V Centaurus has grown compared to the Mk IV series. Is there any difference in handling, flight experience, or range? Yes. The Mk V is tuned to a heavier class than the Mk IV, so it turns and accelerates more slowly, needing more room to reposition in a fight. In exchange, it is far more durable, carries a second S3 shield generator, and reaches a higher NAV speed.

Are there any changes to the weaponry and armor compared to the Mk IV series? The pilot retains control of four S5 weapons as on the Mk IV, but the turrets have been upgraded to quad S3 mounts and are now remote controlled from the bridge by separate crew members.

The missile loadout has been consolidated from four racks of mixed sizes into two racks of matching size, for a total of 32 S2 missiles, with internal storage racks directly behind them so the crew can reload in flight (as on the Perseus).

Armor has also been reinforced: deflection is higher and overall armor integrity is up as well. However, it remains less heavily armored than dedicated warships, such as the Hammerhead and Perseus.

Has anything changed with bridge visibility or landing gear placement? The bridge is all new though retains the spirit of the original, with the crew all sat in one room. The original ship’s struts have also been removed to provide a much improved view.

The landing gear mimics the original’s and the landed pose is clearly a nod back to its forebear, albeit with updated visual design.

The Constellation Mk V Centaurus comes with a snub fighter, the Skylark. Can you tell us more about it? The Skylark is the dedicated snub fighter for the Mk V Centaurus. It features a prone pilot position to keep the ship as slim as possible while packing 3x S2 weapons, a bespoke pair of 5xS1 missile racks, and fully accessible components. The Skylark's inventory and weapon rack can be interacted with while docked within the Constellation Mk V as well as when landed separately.

Unusually for its class, it runs two shield generators rather than one, giving it considerably more staying power than a typical snub. That resilience and capacity come at a price though, as the Skylark sits at the heavier, less agile end of the snub bracket.

When will the Skylark become available as an individual pledge? The RSI Skylark is planned to be introduced as a standalone ship at this year's Intergalactic Aerospace Expo (IAE).

With the recently introduced refuel, rearm, and repair feature for motherships, will the Constellation Mk V Centaurus be able to do the same for the Skylark? No, the Constellation Mk V Centaurus does not have this functionality.

Is the snub docking compatible with the Kruger P-52 Merlin and P-72 Archimedes, or is it exclusive to the Skylark? No, the Skylark is the only ship that can currently dock to the Mk V due to the radically different geometry between the two.

Are there any plans for more Constellation Mk V variants in the future? Yes, we have plans to introduce further variants in the future, covering both familiar and new roles.

body_html:
xē'suelen nyahyan, hello everyone,

Last week, we kicked off RSI Discovery Month, celebrating the legendary Constellation and welcoming the next generation of this iconic ship series. Throughout Stanton, you can visit special RSI installations showcasing the history of the Mk IV and its successor, alongside the new Skylark. Take on a variety of activities, earn exclusive RSI-themed rewards and even complete the special "Constellation Rental Offer" to receive five days of access to put the new Constellation Mk V Centaurus through its paces! Don't forget to share your feedback on Spectrum with our devs.

Spooky season also got a head start with October's Subscriber Promotions: new skeletal-themed flair, including a rifle, suit, and helmet, while the Vehicles of the Month feature Drake's tiny but fierce Pitbull and the formidable Ironclad Assault.

We published the latest PU Monthly Report, offering a behind-the-scenes look at what our teams have been working on throughout September. From Core Gameplay and ship development to technology, art, and more.

The Roadmap Update brought new images for Nyx I-III and introduced a new card for Alpha 4.11: DGS Planet Subdivision, which you can learn more about on the Release View!

This past weekend marked Star Citizen's birthday on October 10, but it was also a very special milestone for Squadron 42 as we welcomed around 140 community members to Manchester for the first hands-on experience.

As we get closer to Squadron 42's launch, our community is going to grow. A lot. There will be countless new faces discovering this universe for the very first time, and we couldn't be more excited to welcome them. But there's something incredibly important to us that we'll never lose sight of: the community that helped get us here.

The Bar Citizen organizers who bring people together all over the world. The artists, crafters, and LEGO® shipbuilders who bring our universe into their own. The loremasters who know more about the 'verse than some of us do! The content creators, the volunteers, the longtime supporters, and the countless Citizens who have spent years welcoming newcomers, guiding rookie pilots, and building something special together.

These are the people who have helped make this project so much more than a game.

We wish we could have invited every single one of you. There are so many incredible people in this community, and 140 guests doesn't even begin to scratch the surface. We hope this weekend was just the beginning of many moments we'll get to celebrate together as we get closer to launch.

Attendees spent five hours playing Squadron 42, followed by an additional hour experiencing a unique chapter of the story aboard an adrift Xi'an ship. If you had a keen eye during CitizenCon Manchester 2954, you might have already caught a glimpse of it! That moment gave me chills, especially as a Xi'an nya'to.y'an (teacher). As our guests make their way home, we're sure you'll hear plenty more about their experiences directly from them.

We're getting closer to the day when Squadron 42 will be in the hands of pilots everywhere. Thank you for being part of this journey. We can't wait for what's to come.

For now, enjoy the Squadron 42 Trailer, and Wishlist on Steam! We'll be sharing photos from the weekend Squadron 42 event soon, so keep an eye on our channels!

Now let's see what's going on this week:

We're celebrating RSI Discovery Month and the legacy of the iconic Constellation with a new round of Twitch Drops. From October 14 to 27, watch any Drops-enabled Star Citizen stream for a total of four hours to unlock the Phoenix Insignia Display for free.

This Tuesday, we'll be releasing the October Monthly Bundle, bringing another selection of gear and goodies. If you like a weathered black and gold finish with ethereal geometric etchings like I do, you'll be in for a treat!

Then, on Wednesday, Behind the Ships returns with a closer look at some of the new ships from Alpha 4.10.2! Join us as we explore what's coming to the 'verse, and take a look at the design process.

On Friday, the latest RSI Weekly Newsletter also lands in your inbox. If you’re not subscribed yet, you can sign up at any time through your account settings.

title: Star Citizen Monthly Report: September 2026
summary: PU Monthly Report September 2026 Welcome to September’s PU Monthly Report, featuring the latest updates from all the various disciplines working on Star Citizen. Read on for all the news from AI Features and Tech, Ships, Community, Core Gameplay, and more.
body_html:
PU Monthly Report September 2026 Welcome to September’s PU Monthly Report, featuring the latest updates from all the various disciplines working on Star Citizen. Read on for all the news from AI Features and Tech, Ships, Community, Core Gameplay, and more.

AI Content

September saw AI Content looking into a new character type for mission gameplay, which will provide additional interactions and personality. They also continued supporting several upcoming missions, adding comms for the new faction reps that have been working their way through the pipeline.

Alongside supporting the social AI placement on planets, the team looked at the existing landing zones to assess what’s working, what isn’t, and how they can make targeted changes to help push each location closer toward the identity established in lore.

AI (Features & Tech)

AI Features and Tech worked on the apex valakkar, committing targeting fixes and bullet-bending refinements. A backstop timer was also introduced when the creature turns to face the player before submerging and emerging to avoid it getting locked.

The team also worked on a number of issues related to Starchitect. For example, ensuring NPCs perform night-time checks and have their flashlights out, and that marok boids spawn correctly. They also improved the nav-mesh to ensure it works with the recent zone changes, including adding a navigation component back to sector clusters.

Animation

Last month, animations were worked on for the apex valakkar, including for major attacks on ship targets. The team also created enter and exit animations for an all-new ship.

Art (Characters)

Last month, Character Art had the final review of a new heavy armor releasing in Alpha 4.10.2. Variations of this will be available as a Wikelo reward and in the store. This release will also include updated brows in the character customizer.

The team is also working on updates to various gangs that will be appearing in Nyx, including First Legion, Salamanders, Shattered Blades, and Moraine. New armor sets will be coming for the First Legion and Salamanders too.

Art (Ships)

In the UK, two unannounced vehicles both had final reviews ahead of their planned release alongside Genesis. Following this, five new projects were kicked off; the first of which made rapid progress considering its size and design.

The second moved through whitebox ahead of its gate review at the end of the month. Following feedback, changes were made to the placement of its main turret and external tractor beam.

The third entered pre-production ahead of its official kick-off, while the fourth and fifth (a pair of ships from a manufacturer not heard from for a while) entered whitebox.

Work also continued on a ship mentioned in recent reports. Last month, it passed through greybox, with the interior now ready for its LOD0 gate review. The exterior is catching up and will be ready for review in early October.

Alongside unannounced vehicles, greybox work on the Anvil Liberator wrapped up, with the formal gate review due in early October. Large areas of the ship that were safe to continue with progressed well into the LOD0 phase, which is due to wrap up in late October.

The RSI Constellation Mk IV Gold Standard progressed, with the devs working through the significant number of minor visual issues across the four variants caused by updating the ship to modern material libraries. They also made user-experience improvements to navigating around and interacting with the ship, with better and more logical placements.

The RSI Galaxy passed its greybox gate review. The team then progressed with LOD0 work, including refining the corridor and wall sections, updating lighting, and adding signage across the ship. Work continued on the modules too.

Finally for the UK, a new ship saw downstream teams, such as UI, VFX, and Audio, do their passes ahead of a combined LOD0/Final review in October.

In North America, production on a new ship wrapped up following internal testing and bug fixing.

Lastly, the Kraken team continued through the LOD0 phase, with efforts spread across the entire ship, from the setup of the integrated transport, like lifts and the tram, to the dedicated capital components located across multiple engineering rooms.

Art (Weapons)

The Weapon Content team completed a new Lightning Bolt Co. rifle alongside paints for upcoming events.

They also continued with seven upcoming weapons, including rifles and a medical pistol, and began updating several ship weapons.

They’re currently planning for 2027, keeping new technology and manufacturer possibilities in mind, and fixing bugs on recently released weapons.

Community

The Community team kicked off an activity-filled September by announcing Ship Showdown 2956's champion, the RSI Perseus. They also published the August Monthly PU Report and began planning for the many events coming throughout autumn and the remainder of the year.

September included the launch of Alpha 4.10: Orison Relief Support, which the team supported with an FAQ outlining how players could take part in rebuilding after the Nine Tails’ attacks. They also published a Q&A for Alpha 4.10’s new vehicles, the Sabre Raven EX and Argo ATLS IKTI Akuma, with answers from the developers themselves.

As Pirate Week sailed into port last month, the team held a treasure hunt with clues hidden across several channels hinting at in-game locations. The team provided a catch-all thread that was updated with the latest clues to the hunt throughout the event. They also challenged the community to flaunt their nefarious deeds by creating custom wanted posters in the Pirate Week 2026 Most Wanted Contest.

Additionally, the Community team gathered questions in preparation for 10 From the Community, a new focused video format where every episode features a few developers representing a particular area of development, including gameplay, art, UI, technology, and ships. They also published an RSI Aurora Mk I Retirement Reminder thread and an FAQ explaining the updates to pledge gifting and game access. These changes are in preparation for the new Game Library system launching in October as part of the broader work to create a clearer and more consistent account experience for both Squadron 42 and Star Citizen.

The Bar Citizen World Tour continued with stops in Seattle for PAX West, as well as Milan, Italy, and Porto, Portugal. Preparation continued for October’s Squadron 42 event, where a group of original backers and content creators will get the chance to try the game for the first time.

As always, the team continued gathering feedback from the community, which is shared with the relevant development teams to ensure players’ voices are heard. They also kept up their regular cadence of This Week in Star Citizen and bi-weekly Roadmap updates, providing the community with the latest information from the development teams throughout an eventful September.

Core Gameplay

The last couple of months saw the Core Gameplay teams working through a long list of bugs and quality-of-life items, many of which were highlighted in the Improving the Live Experience Comm-Link.

For vehicle gameplay, refueling now correctly accounts for the position of the docking connection when ships dock to refuel.

The team also fixed fuel nozzles dumping fuel when a transaction was cancelled, and an issue where mismatched item types caused problems with ship engineering screens. Several other issues were also dealt with, including being unable to repair the Grey’s Market Basher at landing pads, modules failing to equip to ships, shields not recharging after crossing a server boundary, on-foot and vehicle compasses reading differently when in a pilot seat, and ship services failing once started.

Alongside this, some newer ships will now become disabled when a critical part is destroyed rather than exploding immediately. Radar can also detect contacts across the connected areas of a location rather than only within the immediate area.

The team finalized Instancing, releasing it in the Alpha 4.10 patch. As part of this, the devs closed several gaps that allowed players who weren't eligible to pass through instance barriers. Now, loading barriers check directly whether the instance has loaded in before letting players through. Removing a player from an instance is also more reliable when the player and the instance are on different servers.

Instancing respawn queues were also reworked. For example, if a respawn bed is occupied, players now spawn next to it, matching how ship medical beds work. Instances now recover more reliably after a server crash or when control passes between servers, and unload when players take an elevator away from them.

The team began research and investigation into porting Instancing technology to Instanced Hangars.

The transport system now prioritizes empty carriages, reducing the chance of summoning one already in use. The setup of the transport and elevator systems were also simplified.

Freight elevators received attention throughout August and September, with various issues being fixed. These include kiosks getting stuck when transferring items in a loop and becoming unusable, Levski’s external elevators behaving as if they were in zero gravity, elevators becoming unusable after trying to retrieve items that weren't requested, newly split item stacks not being tracked correctly during retrieval, and elevators and their doors showing the wrong visual state when loading in and out.

The team added a limit to loose items, as redeeming very large numbers of small items (e.g. 20,000 water bottles) could crash the kiosk. Kiosks now display this limit and show a clear error when it's exceeded.

Missions that need several of the same items can now accept them all in one hand-in, rather than one at a time. Work began on freight elevator loading messages to show the progress of storing and retrieving items too.

For quantum travel and the Starmap, the devs restored collision checks, so routes can no longer pass straight through moons and other large objects.

Space stations blocking Star Map routes when plotting from inside them was fixed, alongside route markers disappearing between destinations and missing markers when routing to rest stops or jump points. A rare issue where a ship could become unresponsive after quantum travel in poor network conditions was solved too. Routes in Stanton can now also go around the sun.

Support was given for Starchitect missions. Players can now accept them directly from mission boards, and rewards are being connected to them. Resource locations can now be shared across multiple active missions, with each mission set to use an exact or ranged amount, while missions with randomized flows can now end on a random outcome, not just move on to a new phase.

Trespass areas not working at Starchitect locations were fixed too.

Updates were made to the Battaglia mission pack. For example, mining missions can now track rocks destroyed by overcharging. The teams fixed a trigger that blocked progression when entering the mission instance, the delivery stage not completing inside the instance, and an issue where the second and third story missions wouldn’t generate due to an entity ID mismatch when multiple shards were active.

Cargo, trading, and hauling missions were supported throughout the past two months. As part of this, cargo pickups are now distributed more sensibly based on each pickup's SCU. Numerous bugs were also fixed for these missions. These include incorrect item spawn and delivery counts in hauling missions, buying certain commodities blocking the purchase of others, the MISC Hull C failing to auto-load while in loading zones, and fixed ore sales failing at commodity traders.

For ship loss and retrieval, Core Gameplay solved the underlying cause of vehicles occasionally disappearing while being flown in or near hangars.

Retrieved ships sometimes spawning while still in a quantum-travel state was also solved, as was retrieved ships sometimes having their landing gear stuck in the hangar, preventing take-off.

Finally for Core Gameplay, various inventory bugs were fixed, such as the filter and sort menus not closing properly and overlapping with other elements. They also fixed keycards being equippable, which made them disappear into a hidden slot in the player’s inventory, and Stack All appearing to work and then reverting shortly afterwards. Loadouts not sorting inventory items, being unable to place an item after picking it up, the inventory not being restored when leaving prison, and splitting item stacks causing the inventory to become unresponsive were all fixed too.

Mission Design

Last month, the Mission team rebalanced Bounty missions to bring them more in line with the recent ship updates. This will be committed to the game in a future patch.

A new analytics page was set up so the team can more accurately read and parse data and see UEC and engagement imbalances.

Progress was made on a suite of over 97 new contracts for a future patch, which the devs are very excited about, as it changes the way citizens will play.

Two new factions were recently signed off for development, which represent new non-combat-focused careers.

The team also shipped Battaglia and their initial mining missions alongside Orison Relief Support and the first dedicated crafting mission. The Siege of Orison also returned, utilizing the new Instancing tech.

Narrative

In a very productive month, the Narrative team worked on several upcoming mission packs. In addition to a special event that will be making its debut soon, they continued to help with the multitude of contracts that will become available when Nyx I is released.

Narrative also revised the script for an upcoming story mission that will feature multiple new characters, and began coordinating on new contracts that will expand what missions InterSec offers to mercenary-minded players.

As they often do this time of year, Narrative supported the upcoming Intergalactic Aerospace Expo with new additions. Additionally, work continued on the loading screen headlines that will be featured in upcoming patches.

Online Technology

Live Tools completed part two of the Hex 4.0 feature-parity work. For this, they rebuilt the account detail and listing pages (quick view, rental history, tabbed tables), added group detail views with chat, and reached parity on dataset and chat export. They also completed a UI polish pass, including the search page, drag-and-drop tabs, header support link, and quick view.

For Bootstrap, the devs closed the client-revamp initiation phase, with the technology stack chosen and proof-of-concept built. The client rebuild is now underway.

Live Tools also progressed with Error Reporting, adding advanced crash-listing filters (by type and status) and further pipeline reliability work, including a scheduled Panic Switch database cleanup. Work on crash-pipeline reliability, enrichment, and Panic Switch polish continued.

The Online Services team spent much of September improving the reliability of missions and contracts. They fixed a bug where a mix-up in reputation data could cause players to occasionally be shown the wrong mission, and worked through ongoing efforts to reduce delays players experience before new contracts are available to accept. The team also continued refining how ‘Contract No Longer Available’ errors are communicated to players, aiming for clearer, more immersive in-game messaging instead of generic error text.

The Network team's biggest focus was building a new system called Claims; a smarter way for the game to decide which servers are responsible for which parts of the universe. This includes planets, activities, and instanced events. This groundwork lays the foundation for the servers to handle territory assignments more flexibly and reliably going forward. The team also made progress on grouping instanced activities by their type, so the game can better tailor how content streams in depending on what kind of event or location a player is in.

Alongside this core work, the team continued auditing the network code to prepare for more advanced streaming support. On the reliability side, the team investigated and addressed a warning tied to how debris behaves when a ship is destroyed inside enclosed spaces, like hangars. Finally, several smaller networking code cleanups and performance improvements were completed as part of the team's regular upkeep work.

R&D

The R&D team progressed with volumetric clouds, fixing an issue with occasional stale cloud shadow maps after fast camera movement. Stochastic cloud shadow map filtering was also improved.

Significant work also went into render modes. As part of this, a new quarter-res render mode was added as a non-temporal performance mode, and a new unified guide was introduced covering the half, quarter, and temporal render modes. Filter improvements for the half and quarter res modes now better reconstruct the thin atmosphere silhouette when viewed from far orbit. Within the temporal render mode, the motion sensitivity term was reworked and scene visibility awareness was added to the temporal up-sampling along with the neighborhood bbox hull. Ongoing work included VGPR reductions for the spatio-temporal upsampler, and general cloud ray marcher optimizations.

Shadow map encoding was also improved to reduce occasional banding, which was especially visible on terrain covered by thin ground fog under a low sun angle.

On the integration side, all weather improvements from the past few months, as well as atmosphere and cloud rendering, merged into the development streams. This included fixes for issues found in integration reviews and a follow-up change to migrate the integrated work so it handles and supports streaming of atmosphere, ground fog, and cloud resources.

Finally, investigation began into a proper solution for sky irradiance to take cloud coverage into account, which remains in progress. On the planet atmosphere side, work continued on injecting clouds into the atmosphere model.

title: This Week in Star Citizen
summary: xē'suelen nyahyan, hello everyone,
body_html:
xē'suelen nyahyan, hello everyone,

Last week was a busy one on the testing front, with plenty of you jumping into both the Tech Preview and Alpha 4.10.2 PTU.

We put the latest Physicalized Entity Netcode overhaul through its paces, and we’ve been encouraged by the early response while also collecting plenty of notes for further improvements ahead of its release in an upcoming update. Ship TTK balancing was also part of the weekend’s tests, and our teams are now digging through your feedback and data as we continue tuning the experience, including the AI modifier for PvE.

We also appreciate all the early feedback on Alpha 4.10.2’s new in-system event. Testing will continue with additional PTU builds as we make further additions, address issues, and refine the experience based on what we’re seeing and hearing from you. As always, if you encounter a bug or have feedback to share, please keep it coming through the Issue Council and our dedicated Spectrum feedback threads. Thank you to everyone spending time testing with us!

If you missed the announcement last week, we’re introducing 10 From the Community, a brand-new show debuting on October 5. Short, focused, and driven by your questions, each episode will tackle a different area of Star Citizen development. Head over to the announcement on Spectrum to submit your questions for the first episode, and don’t forget to vote for the ones you most want to see answered.

Finally this past weekend, we had an incredible time at Bar Citizen Porto, and it was fantastic to meet so many of you, swap stories, hear your feedback, and spend an evening together. Thank you to everyone who came out and made it a night to remember. Vamos!

Now let's see what's going on this week:

TWITCH DROPS: RSI DISCOVERY MONTH

From October 14 to 27, celebrate RSI Discovery Month and the legacy of the Constellation by watching any Drops-enabled Star Citizen stream for a total of four hours to unlock the Phoenix Insignia Display for free. Inspired by the signature fiery insignia found aboard the classic Constellation Phoenix, this holographic display brings a piece of RSI history straight to your hangar.

From October 14 to 27, celebrate RSI Discovery Month and the legacy of the Constellation by watching any Drops-enabled Star Citizen stream for a total of four hours to unlock the Phoenix Insignia Display for free. Inspired by the signature fiery insignia found aboard the classic Constellation Phoenix, this holographic display brings a piece of RSI history straight to your hangar.

TWITCH DROPS:

RSI DISCOVERY MONTH

From October 14 to 27, celebrate RSI Discovery Month and the legacy of the Constellation by watching any Drops-enabled Star Citizen stream for a total of four hours to unlock the Phoenix Insignia Display for free. Inspired by the signature fiery insignia found aboard the classic Constellation Phoenix, this holographic display brings a piece of RSI history straight to your hangar.

Link Your Twitch & RSI Accounts

To start earning Twitch Drops, you’ll need to link your Twitch account to your existing RSI account. This only takes a few minutes and ensures your earned rewards are delivered directly to your Hangar.

Here’s how to link your accounts:

1. Go to your RSI Account Settings:

Log in to the RSI website.

Open your Account Dashboard.

Click Settings, then select Linked Accounts.

2. Link your Twitch account:

In Linked Accounts settings, you’ll see options such as Google and Twitch.

Click the Twitch button which will redirect you to the Twitch login page.

Log in to your Twitch account and authorize the connection when prompted.

Once linked, you can now watch any Star Citizen stream with Drops enabled to start earning rewards.

Link Your Twitch & RSI AccountsTo start earning Twitch Drops, you’ll need to link your Twitch account to your existing RSI account. This only takes a few minutes and ensures your earned rewards are delivered directly to your Hangar. Here’s how to link your accounts: 1. Go to your RSI Account Settings: Log in to the RSI website. Open your Account Dashboard. Click Settings, then select Linked Accounts. 2. Link your Twitch account: In Linked Accounts settings, you’ll see options such as Google and Twitch. Click the Twitch button which will redirect you to the Twitch login page. Log in to your Twitch account and authorize the connection when prompted. Once linked, you can now watch any Star Citizen stream with Drops enabled to start earning rewards.

FAQ

FAQ What are Twitch Drops? Twitch Drops are rewards that players can earn by watching participating Twitch streams. When you link your Star Citizen account to your Twitch account and watch any eligible Star Citizen stream for 4 hours, you’ll automatically unlock in-game items as rewards. Once you meet the watch-time requirement, your reward will appear in your Twitch inventory and can then be claimed to your Star Citizen account.

For this campaign, the featured reward is the Phoenix Insignia Display.

How long will the current campaign last? This Drops campaign runs from October 14 through October 27. Make sure to tune in to eligible streams or subscribe to a participating creator before the campaign ends.

How do I participate? To participate, you need to link your Twitch and RSI accounts (see above for instructions).

Then watch any Star Citizen live stream marked “Drops Enabled.”

Once you’ve watched for 4 hours, claim your Drop on Twitch. It will appear in your RSI Hangar shortly after.

Which live streams count toward earning Drops? Any Star Citizen stream on Twitch marked "Drops Enabled" counts toward the reward. Starting October 14, with the launch of RSI Discovery Month, any community streamer who opts in to Twitch Drops will be eligible to host the campaign and have their viewers earn rewards.

How can I check my progress or claim a Drop? You can track your progress on the Twitch Drops Inventory page while logged in to your Twitch account.

When your watch-time or subscription goal is complete, click “Claim” on Twitch to receive the Drop.

Do I need Amazon Luna (Prime Gaming) to be eligible? No. You don't need Amazon Luna or Prime Gaming. A regular Twitch account linked to your RSI account is all you need to participate.

Can I unlink or relink my Twitch account? Yes. You can unlink your Twitch account anytime from your RSI Account Settings under Linked Accounts. To relink, simply repeat the connection process shown above.

Can I link multiple Twitch accounts to one RSI account, or multiple RSI accounts to one Twitch account? No. Each RSI account can be linked to only one Twitch account, and vice versa. If you want to connect to a different account, you’ll need to unlink the previous account first.

My Drop didn’t appear in my RSI account. What should I do? First, make sure you:

Linked the correct Twitch and RSI accounts.

Watched streams or subscribed using the linked Twitch account.

Claimed the Drop on Twitch.

Are logging into the correct RSI account.

If the Drop still hasn’t appeared after a while but it is showing that it has unlocked on Twitch, please contact Player Support for assistance.

title: This Week in Star Citizen
summary: Happy Monday, everyone!
body_html:
Happy Monday, everyone!

Last week, Alpha 4.10.1 arrived on our Live servers, introducing Orison Relief Support alongside the new Aegis Sabre Raven EX. From now until October 7, you can help rebuild Orison from the ashes through various missions, from combat and salvage to crafting and hauling supplies where they're needed most, with a full set of "SecondWind" gear waiting for those who see it through. If you have questions about Orison Relief Support or the new vehicles, be sure to check out the Orison Relief Support FAQ and Vehicle Q&A Comm-Link.

Thank you to everyone who tested throughout the PTU phase and helped push Alpha 4.10.1 out the door. A big shoutout as well to everyone who jumped into the Time-to-Kill Balance Test Tech-Preview, your feedback continues to shape how combat feels across the 'verse. With that said, there's more testing ahead: Alpha 4.10.2 will begin Evocati PTU testing shortly, with wider waves to follow. As always, if you run into any bugs or have feedback, don't forget to report them through the Issue Council and the dedicated Spectrum feedback threads. We appreciate your support.

Speaking of keeping busy, Pirate Week 2026 is far from over. There's still time to make a name for yourself in the Most Wanted contest and let the 'verse know who to fear. And for those chasing bigger treasure, the hunt for the "doubloon" draws to a close, with the final clue hidden within this very page for only those sharp enough to spot it.

Following up on our earlier announcement about changes to pledge gifting and game access, we have published an FAQ explaining how the new Game Library system will work when it takes effect on October 1, 2026. Also, you'll be able to select your preferred pledge for the new system during a window running through November 1. Read the full details here.

Last but not least, huge thanks to everyone who joined us for Bar Citizen Milan! It was a fantastic night filled with laughs, quizzes, giveaways, and plenty of great conversations with passionate pilots, all brought together by our shared love for Star Citizen. A special shoutout to TileMiaRut for organizing such an amazing event. You made the whole team feel right at home!

Now, let's see what's going on this week:

Today, we’re introducing 10 From the Community, a new show debuting on October 5. It’ll be short, focused, and built around your questions, with each episode covering a different area of Star Citizen’s development. Head over to today’s announcement to submit your questions for the first episode, and remember to vote for the ones you most want to see answered.

At the same time, we’re taking a wider look at our show lineup and the kinds of content we produce. We’ll be sharing a survey soon to hear what you’d like to see from us. Whether there’s an old favorite you’d love to see return or an entirely new idea you think we should explore, we want to hear it.

Wednesday would normally bring the latest Roadmap Update and Roadmap Roundup, but with Alpha 4.11 development on track and no notable changes to report this week, we've decided to hold off for now and revisit the Roadmap Update in two weeks.

Friday, the RSI Weekly Newsletter lands in your inbox as usual. If you're not subscribed yet, you can sign up anytime through your account settings.

On Saturday, September 26, we're heading to Porto, Portugal, for our next Bar Citizen World Tour stop! Join us at MXM ArtCenter from 2:00 PM to 7:00 PM UTC for an evening with fellow Citizens and the development team. We can't wait to see you there!

Also on Saturday, the Fight or Flight 2956 3v3 dogfighting tournament reaches its finals! Don't forget to catch the best squads in the 'verse going head-to-head as they battle it out for the championship.

Finally, before you go, a quick hello: this is Steve, also known on Spectrum as Stamp-CIG. Some of you may recognize me from running various Spectrum contests, and I've had the pleasure of meeting quite a few of you in person at past Bar Citizen events. I've mostly been working behind the scenes supporting the team, and I'm now taking on TWISC on a rotating basis as well. As a player and lifelong fan of Star Citizen myself, this game means a lot to me, and being part of this community is something I genuinely enjoy. Looking forward to bringing you more news and updates down the line, and I will see you in the 'verse!

Cheers,

AN ICON OF SPACE TRAVEL

Humanity has always looked to the stars to find its way. For generations of pilots, the Constellation has helped chart the course. From exploration and commerce to combat and comfort, the Aquila, Taurus, Andromeda, and Phoenix have each built a story of their own.

Now, newly updated with a host of quality of life additions that keep this storied legend at it's peak, the Mk IV leaves the production line as a modern classic, destined to be prized by pilots who know its worth.

Better Than Ever

To commemorate the Constellation Mk IV’s transition to modern classic, RSI has released a series of major upgrades across all four variants, including improved bridge visibility, redesigned habitation areas, additional suit lockers and weapon racks, full component access and more, while the extravagant Phoenix has received additional luxury touches throughout.

summary: RSI DISCOVERY MONTH
body_html:
RSI DISCOVERY MONTH

To commemorate its inspiring legacy of exploration, RSI invites pilots across Stanton to join it in celebrating the arrival of the next-generation Constellation, the new Mk V Centaurus.

Located throughout the system, discover special RSI installations dedicated to the legendary history of the Constellation Mk IV and the brand-new Mk V (plus its companion, the Skylark). Features and Gameplay Introducing new features while updating and refining existing functionality.

Gameplay: Orison Relief Support - Ground Vehicle Soft Death - Loot Quality and Attachment Availability Orison Relief Support

Crusader Industries' relief initiative is now live. In the wake of the Nine Tails attack, Orison needs rebuilding and its defenses need upgrading, and Crusader is paying anyone willing to help.

Contracts come from four providers. Cornerstone Developments handles reconstruction, running resource gathering work into Orison and Seraphim alongside a crafted aid line built around the TH-01 Propulsor. Covalex and Ling cover the medical response, collecting medical supplies and iodine from New Babbage, the New Babbage rooftops and Port Tressler for delivery into Orison, the Orison rooftops and Seraphim. Foxwell handles security, with ship ambush and wave attack contracts in space and an Eliminate All contract clearing Nine Tails out of outposts on foot.

Every contract you complete feeds your own progress track rather than paying out in isolation. Progress is personal, so you are working toward your own rewards at your own pace, and each reward is granted straight to your account as you pass its threshold. Six rewards are on offer, unlocking in this order:

S-38 "SecondWind" Pistol

FBL-8a SecondWind Light Armor

P4-AR "SecondWind" Rifle

ORC-mkX SecondWind Medium Armor

Lumin V "SecondWind" SMG

ADP-mk4 SecondWind Heavy Armor

Rewards are granted as finished items rather than as blueprints to craft. Points earned on a contract completed as a party are divided between the party members.

The crafted aid line needs an Item Fabricator. The TH-01 Propulsor blueprint is attached to the contract and can be found on the fabricator's own terminal, which will list the materials required. If you do not own a fabricator yet you will need to buy one from a shop, unload it at a freight elevator and set it up in a hangar or a ship's cargo bay.

Ground Vehicle Soft Death

Ground vehicles can now enter the soft death state, bringing them in line with ships. A disabled ground vehicle will now be left inert rather than going straight from working to destroyed.

Creature and Plant Loot Quality

Loot harvested from creatures and plants now comes in graded quality brackets. Kopion horns, Marok pearls, Valakkar fangs and pearls, Yormandi eyes, Quasigrazer eggs and tongues, gasping weevil eggs and ranta dung are all covered, alongside a wide range of harvestable plants including spiral fruit, sunset berries, jumping limes, degnous root and heart of the woods. What you bring back is worth checking before you sell it or craft with it.

Weapon Attachment Availability

Barrel compensators and stabilizers across all three sizes are now available from the general loot pool rather than being restricted to a narrow set of sources, so attachments turn up far more reliably while looting.

Hauling and Delivery Cargo Distribution

The way contract cargo is distributed across pickup locations has been reworked. Multi-pickup contracts now account for the SCU weight of each individual pickup when splitting a load, so cargo is spread across the markers the contract actually gives you instead of stacking into a single inventory, and percentile-based cargo amounts now resolve correctly.

Audio

Spaceship and shared audio work has been brought forward into this build, along with an Aegis Sabre series audio remake

Audio has been added for the AMRS S3 and S4 laser cannons

Bug Fixes & Technical Updates

For a comprehensive up to date list of Known issues and Workarounds, please check out our Knowledge Base here!

Alpha 4.10.1 closes 37 issues, with a focus on problems that could cost you an entire session. These include contract cargo spawning in the wrong location, vehicles that couldn’t be retrieved from ASOP terminals, freight elevators getting stuck mid-transfer, and multiple exploits.

16 of those 37 fixes came through the Issue Council, and each one includes a link to the original report. Your reports, confirmations, and reproduction steps help us reliably recreate issues and prioritize them alongside everything else.

Many of the fixes in this patch were pinned down thanks to players providing detailed information from different angles. Thank you to everyone who took the time to contribute!

Client Crashes: 3

Server crashes: 2

Client crashes fixed

Fixed a crash that could occur while characters and creatures were being animated on screen. The renderer could release a character's mesh while that same mesh was still being deformed for the frame being drawn.

Resolved a crash that occurred as an object registered itself with the system that tracks which part of the world it belongs to. If the object and its parent disagreed about what they were attached to, which could happen with items and components mounted on a ship, the mismatch would take the client down.

Fixed a crash while calculating an object's position, rotation and scale in the world, triggered by an object being left with an invalid transform.

Missions

Hauling and cargo contracts

Fixed an issue where multi-pickup contract cargo could all sit in a single pickup location's inventory despite the contract showing several pickup markers STARC-202557

Resolved an issue where some hauling contracts would not spawn enough cargo at the collect locations STARC-217295

Fixed an issue where Covalex delivery contracts would not spawn the full amount of cargo for pickup STARC-206770

The three hauling and cargo fixes came out of larger distribution work for 4.10.1. Contract cargo distribution was reworked because the old code split a load across pickup locations without accounting for how much each individual pickup was actually carrying, so it could put everything in one place while still handing you several markers. Alongside that, percentile based cargo amounts were resolving incorrectly, cargo generation had an off by one error, and nothing validated that the number of dropoffs matched the number of pickups. Distribution now weights each pickup by its SCU, the percentile and off by one errors are fixed, and a mismatch between pickup and dropoff counts now raises an error rather than generating a contract you cannot finish.

Refuelling contracts

Fixed an issue where the contract details listed the wrong amount of fuel, and introductory refuelling contracts asked for quantum fuel as well as hydrogen STARC-218420Introductory refuelling contracts were asking for quantum fuel as well as hydrogen, so the amount shown in the contract never matched the job in front of you. Those contracts now ask for hydrogen only.

Corrected an issue where the refuelling interface displayed the wrong price per SCU of fuel

Other mission content

Fixed an issue where the Tactical Strike Group Full Strike contract would not progress past the Go To Objective step STARC-218828The mission logic could not find the harvestable container it was looking for at the objective, so the step never registered as complete and the contract stalled there permanently.

Resolved an issue where the Nine Tails commander in Siege of Orison was equipped with the wrong heavy machine gun variant

Locations and Environment

Stanton locations

Fixed an issue where armistice zones were missing throughout Orison STARC-217142Orison's armistice areas were being skipped while the game worked out which zones were active, which left the whole location without weapon restrictions. Area resolution has been corrected so the armistice zones apply again.

Pyro

Fixed an issue where the irradiated Valakkar egg would not appear at the Lazarus Complex STARC-192834The egg nursery was running on a reset cycle far longer than the window players were arriving in, so the egg was usually absent. The nursery now resets on a much shorter cycle.

Ships and Vehicles

Flight, damage and components

Fixed an issue where most of the Drake Clipper's hull took no damage, and where the underside doors could not be damaged STARC-219126The Clipper's body had several overlapping collision shapes layered on top of each other, so incoming fire never resolved against the hull itself and the ship read as effectively invulnerable across most of its surface. The duplicates have been removed and the doors on the underside are now proper damageable parts.

Resolved an issue where ground vehicles were unable to enter the soft death stateGround vehicles had no disabled state at all, so they went straight from working to destroyed. They now have one, matching how ships behave.

Fixed a case where ship computer dialogue lines would not play while the player was in the pilot seat STARC-216621

Corrected an issue where the vehicle compass read a different bearing in the pilot seat than it did on foot STARC-103033

Hangars, ASOP, and vehicle retrieval

Both fixes below share a root cause. A vehicle landed inside a hangar was not guaranteed to be put away when that hangar was stowed, streamed out or deleted, so it could be left in a state where neither the hangar nor the terminal considered it dealt with. Vehicles landed inside a hangar now always stow in all three of those cases, and a flag that was failing to clear properly has been fixed, which covered the remaining cases where a vehicle got stuck between being stored and a new ship being spawned.

Fixed an issue where the Retrieve button on ASOP terminals could become greyed out, leaving a vehicle impossible to spawn, retrieve or deliver STARC-214984

Resolved an issue where ships would stay stuck on "moving to storage" if the player streamed out of the hangar while it was still storing STARC-205267

Both of the Air Traffic Control fixes below trace to the same place. The keybinding and the comms call each looked up the nearest ATC contact for themselves, and the lookup used by the keybinding did not handle zone and instance roots correctly, so it frequently found nothing to talk to while the comms call worked fine. That lookup has been corrected, and the keybinding now reaches ATC in the same cases the comms call does.

Fixed an issue where the hotkey to request landing or takeoff from Air Traffic Control did nothing, while the comms call still worked STARC-217211

Resolved an issue where Air Traffic Control could not be contacted at all through its keybinding shortcut

Fixed a problem where the Kruger S-65 Stingray would spawn partly inside the hangar floor

Ship art and liveries

Fixed an issue where equipping certain liveries left the Aegis Sabre's landing gear showing a placeholder textureThe landing gear was built in a format that did not carry the material assignments the liveries needed. It has been rebuilt and its material IDs remapped, with a separate pass to stop overlapping surfaces flickering against each other.

Cargo and Freight Elevators

Fixed an issue where raising a freight elevator at its maximum capacity would leave it stuck in a transferring stateOpening the kiosk while an unstow request was still being processed queued a second request to open the inventory, and the platform was then left waiting on a transfer that never arrived. A guard now blocks that second request until the first has finished.

Resolved an issue where loading platform state recovery could snap the platform into a raised position with cargo still on it and the doors closed STARC-211125

Fixed a case where a delivery failure error would appear when storing cargo left on a freight elevator grid after exiting and returning to the gameThe platform and the server disagreed about the gravity acting on the cargo, which made the stored contents fail validation. The platform now rechecks gravity when the kiosk is opened.

UI

Starmap, markers, and navigation

These two came out of the same investigation. The orbital markers the router uses to plot a path around Stanton's star were disabled, so any route passing near the star failed outright rather than curving around it. Fixing that exposed a second case: the router was not generating points around a space station either, so a destination on the far side of the station you were sitting in would also refuse to set. Both now route correctly.

Fixed an issue where the Starmap would not plot a route around an obstructed path STARC-130415Large bodies sitting between you and your destination, including the Stanton star itself, were treated as hard blockers rather than something to route around, so no course would be set at all.

Resolved an issue where a quantum route could not be set from inside a station to a destination on the far side of it

Main menu and front end

Fixed an issue where a line in the pause menu was out of place

Inventory and Items

Weapons and attachments

Fixed an issue where weapon attachments were missing from the loot pool at Distribution Center delving sites and elsewhere

Armor and clothing

Resolved an issue where the Nine Tails Shogun armor set had no tints available

Fixed an issue where the Nine Tails Shogun armor showed item boxes instead of the armor in inventory previews

Corrected an issue where text on the legs of the September store armor read incorrectly

Props and flair

Fixed an issue where the Bosco weapon display rack did not match its reference image

Corrected a spelling error in the description of the M80 "Beauty Is Power" poster

Fixed by Hotfix Since 4.10.0 Went Live

The following 26 fixes reached the live environment a hotfixes in the weeks after 4.10.0 launched.

Server stability

Fixed a server crash caused by a mission prop sitting in a player's inventory, which could hold a shard in a repeating crash loop for over an hour

Resolved a server crash where the same object could be queued for cleanup twice and deleted twice

Fixed a server crash while looking up a component that had already been released

Resolved a server crash when a ship's thruster was asked for its capacity while its flight system was being torn down

Fixed memory corruption caused by several parts of the game reading a weapon's fire modes at the same time as they were being cleared

Fixed a crash in the physics system when moving through areas exported before a newer collision check existed

Added a limit on how many loose items can be unstowed onto a freight elevator platform at once, which was capable of chain crashing a server

Resolved an issue where entering a vehicle could overwrite the previous driver without clearing them first, putting the client and server out of step

Disconnects

Fixed a family of issues where a server node would shut down immediately and disconnect everyone on itThe server was accepting a confirmation that an object's layout was final without checking that the layout it had actually matched the one being confirmed. When they disagreed, the node exited rather than continuing. It now verifies the layout first. This covered several separate reports, including repeating shutdowns around the Nyx points of interest and a bad variable index on the ARGO MOLE's turrets.

Client crashes

Fixed a client crash in the graphics layer where a texture view could still be in use while it was being discarded, which surfaced after memory defragmentation was introduced

Performance

Resolved an issue where the audio thread could cause significant frame rate drops, and a related audio crash STARC-214091

Improved memory handling for the system that partitions the world into regions, which was allocating and freeing far too often

Restored optimization on a number of files where it had been accidentally left disabled

Missions

Fixed an issue where Battaglia's second and third story contracts were never created on busy shards, leaving players with no follow-up after the first STARC-218134Mission generation was querying locations using stored identifiers that are not valid on every shard, and the caches backing those queries were not being cleared properly when a shard started up. Missions that depended on a Moraine base as their location were the most visible casualty.

Resolved an issue where the Nine Tails commander in Siege of Orison could take collision damage while being teleported between phases, and die instantly

Ships and vehicles

Fixed an issue where a vehicle with an expired idle timer was impounded again within seconds of every retrieval

Items and interface

Fixed an issue where Super Heavy armor could not be unequipped to local inventory if anything was attached to it

Resolved an issue where the mech style footstep audio from the Super Heavy suit kept playing after the armor was unequipped STARC-213441

Fixed an issue where arrow key and gamepad D-pad navigation stopped working in mobiGlas, because a mouse position update sent every frame was clearing the keyboard focus one frame after each press

Visuals

Fixed an issue where holograms could render incorrectly from certain angles when upscaling was enabled

Resolved several water issues, including simulation not running on ships and broken shading on water volumes and rivers

title: Q&A: Aegis Sabre Raven EX and Argo ATLS IKTI Akuma
summary: Q&A Aegis Sabre Raven EX & Argo ATLS IKTI Akuma
body_html:
Q&A Aegis Sabre Raven EX & Argo ATLS IKTI Akuma

We asked the Vehicle team a few questions about the two vehicles releasing with Alpha 4.10.1: Orison Relief Support. Here are the answers, straight from the devs themselves.

Aegis Sabre Raven EX What is a "Quantum Dampener" and how is it different than a "Quantum Snare?" These are two related technologies. A Quantum Dampener (QDMP) prevents ships within range from entering quantum travel. This is useful for keeping your target from escaping the fight. A Quantum Snare can force ships out of quantum travel. Certain ships that have both technologies refer to this as a Quantum Enforcement Device (QED.)

What other ships have a "Quantum Dampener?" As of Alpha 4.10.1, only four other flyable ships have a Quantum Dampener. These are the RSI Mantis, the Drake Cutlass Blue, The RSI Scorpius Antares and the Mirai Guardian QI. Of these, only the Antares and QI are considered "fighters" and only the latter can be operated solo, putting the Aegis Sabre Raven EX in limited company.

How does the performance and capabilities of the Raven EX compare to that of the Sabre and Sabre Raven? The Sabre Raven EX is intended to be a blend of balancing between the two. In weapons, it has the same capabilities as the Sabre with four S3 hardpoints (an improvement over the original Raven) while in speed and maneuverability it falls in between: greater speed than the Sabre and more armor than the Raven, but less stealth emission reduction than the Raven and less agility than the Sabre.

Does this share paints with the other Sabres? Yes, as the sixth variant in the Aegis Sabre lineup, there are a host of paints already available for the new Sabre Raven EX, and the new paints offered in this release will be usable on every Sabre that's come before.

What does this mean for the original Sabre Raven? The original Sabre Raven remains a rare and unique offering within the Star Citizen universe. We're offering the Sabre Raven EX with a different flight role and mission purpose that allows those of you who love the Sabre line but have always wanted the Raven visuals to finally fly the way you want.

Argo ATLS IKTI Akuma How does the Argo ATLS IKTI Akuma differ from the Argo ATLS GEO IKTI we can earn in game? Visually, the differences begin with a unique Nine Tails-inspired default livery. In Gameplay, the mounted weapons have been further customized by the Nine Tails to offer plasma repeaters with splash damage and a jump pack that trades a modest amount of jump height for increased distance and fuel capacity.

Are paints compatible between these variants? As with the Raven EX above, all power suits in the ATLS line share the same paint capability. While the unique Nine-Tails livery is exclusive to the new Akuma, you can use all available ATLS paint past and future on this.

Why is this being offered by pledge and not in-game? When we first added the Argo ATLS GEO IKTI in Alpha 4.2, we made it earnable exclusively in game. While it's important to us that still remains a uniquely available offering, we also understand many folks prefer the comfort of knowing during the Alpha period that they've secured their vehicles permanently. While it is still our intention to keep the original IKTI as it currently is, we felt that adding a variant into an existing armor/weapon/paint store bundle was an interesting opportunity to try something new.

DISCLAIMER These answers accurately reflect development's intentions at the time of writing, but the company and development team reserve the right to adapt, improve, or change feature and ship designs in response to feedback, playtesting, design revisions, or other considerations to improve balance or the quality of the game overall.

We also published a new Roadmap Update, adding the new event Orison Relief Support to Alpha 4.10.1. Head over to the Release View for the latest on what's currently in the works for Alpha 4.11.

Later this week, we're targeting the release of Alpha 4.10.1, bringing another round of technical and bug fixes, including fixes to ASOP terminals and ship statuses, a fix for Mendo Ren's HMG spawn issues, and more. You can follow the current PTU updates on Spectrum.

The update will also introduce the Orison Relief Support event, where you'll lend a hand in rebuilding Orison through missions spanning resource gathering, crafting, hauling, and combat. Following your feedback from the PTU, we've significantly reduced the requirements needed to complete the event, while its blueprints have been removed from the reward track and will instead be granted directly to your account. We'll keep hammering on Alpha 4.10.1 in the PTU ahead of its Live release, while work continues on Alpha 4.11.

If you can't join us in Milan, there are plenty of other Bar Citizen events to check out, organized by fantastic members of the community this Saturday in France (Rouen), Texas (Fort Worth and Austin), and New Mexico (Albuquerque). title: This Week in Star Citizen
summary: Happy Monday, everyone!
body_html:
Happy Monday, everyone!

Last week saw the culmination of the biggest throwdown yet in the clash for aerospace supremacy. Ship Showdown 2956 has its Undisputed Champion of the 'Verse, and it's the RSI Perseus! The gunship ended one more battle in the final, taking down the Drake Ironclad Assault after a fight the crowds are still talking about. [Note to self: rough week to be a Drake girl.] The Origin M80 and the Drake Corsair round out this year's Final Four, due to receive Best In Show honors at this year's Intergalactic Aerospace Expo. You can relive every round at the Ship Showdown hub.

Subscribers also received their exclusive September perks, featuring the Vehicle of the Month ahead: the MISC Freelancer MAX, a long-range hauler built for the dangers of deep-space delivery. Coming along for the ride are decorative display cases for collectors to showcase their loot.

We also published the August PU Monthly Report, with a look at what the dev teams tackled last month, from work that fed into Alpha 4.10: Siege of Orison to what's cooking further down the line.

Lastly, a huge thank you to everyone who came out to the PAX West Bar Citizen in Seattle last Friday. We loved reconnecting with familiar faces and meeting new pilots along the way. The Bar Citizen World Tour rolls on, with our next stop in Milan, Italy, on September 19. We hope to see you there!

Tuesday kicks off the week with the September Monthly bundle comm-link, giving you a look at the armor, weapon, and ship paint bundle coming with Alpha 4.10.1.

Come Wednesday, ready yer crews and hoist the Jolly Roger once more, mateys, for the time be upon us for Pirate Week 2026!

Wednesday also brings the latest Roadmap Update and its complementary Roundup.

Friday will see the RSI Newsletter delivered straight into your inbox with the week's highlights from across the 'verse.

On Saturday, our friends at ATMO esports are giving dogfighters their shot at glory: Fight or Flight kicks off its 2026 season with the EMEA/NA group stage. There's still time to sign up; registration closes midnight UTC on September 11.

Fly low, and fly fast!
