title: Intergalactic Aerospace Expo 2955 Free Fly and Manufacturer Schedule
summary: Intergalactic Aerospace Expo 2955 Free Fly & Manufacturer Schedule Join us in the breathtaking city of Orison, system Stanton, for the biggest spaceship show in the universe! To celebrate the Intergalactic Aerospace Expo 2955, Star Citizen will be FREE TO PLAY throughout the entire event.
body_html:
Intergalactic Aerospace Expo 2955 Free Fly & Manufacturer Schedule Join us in the breathtaking city of Orison, system Stanton, for the biggest spaceship show in the universe! To celebrate the Intergalactic Aerospace Expo 2955, Star Citizen will be FREE TO PLAY throughout the entire event.

From November 20 through December 3, you have the chance to try some of Star Citizen's most iconic vehicles for free. All you have to do is to create an account, download the game and jump into the fun.

Here's how it works:

During the Intergalactic Aerospace Expo, anyone can explore Star Citizen's Persistent Universe for free. Even if you don't have a Star Citizen Game Package, you can try it for free and fly to the in-game event in style with Crusader's light freighter, the Intrepid, which we're loaning to all players for free for the duration of the event.

The event lands in Orison on November 20, 16:00 UTC. Explore the vast expo halls, check out the latest and most iconic vehicles from top manufacturers, and take them out for a spin. New reveals and surprises will debut throughout the event, with free rental access unlocking each day according to the manufacturer schedule.

Check out the schedule below to plan your test flights, and stay up to date with our IAE newsletter! Sign up to receive the latest updates straight to your inbox with news, event highlights, and surprises from the show floor. Got questions? Head over to Spectrum and browse the IAE 2955 FAQ.

Roberts Space Industries Day 1, November 20-21 The Perseus is finally making its debut in the 'verse! This heavy gunship is perfect for those looking to take on large opponents, so don’t miss the chance to give it a try. Check out the Perseus and the rest of RSI’s lineup on Day 1 of IAE:

RSI Perseus - Capable of shredding sub-capital class goliaths, the mere presence of a Perseus gunship in a blockade or patrol squad is enough to make your most aggressive enemies think twice before engaging, just like its vintage namesake.

RSI Salvation - With beginner-friendly functionality and a back-to-basics interior, the Salvation brings exactly that to those dreaming of finding their tomorrow in yesterday’s wrecks.

RSI Apollo Medivac - A life-saving ship with enhanced armor and missile racks, capable of responding to calls in the heaviest combat.

RSI Apollo Triage - The Triage delivers highly configurable, professional-level medical care anywhere in the galaxy.

RSI Aurora CL - The Aurora Clipper is an effective vessel for aspiring entrepreneurs and seasoned traders alike.

RSI Aurora ES - A descendant of the X-7, this is the ideal choice for new ship owners. Versatile and intuitive.

RSI Aurora LN - For combat-focused citizens. The Aurora LN comes with bigger shields and larger weapons that pack a punch.

RSI Aurora LX - The Aurora Deluxe adds luxury and comfort for long stretches into the deep.

RSI Aurora MR - A balance of function and performance, the Aurora MR comes with cargo capacity and guns to ensure freight gets there safely.

RSI Constellation Andromeda - A multi-crew freighter with a modular design, the RSI Andromeda is one of the most iconic ships in the verse.

RSI Constellation Aquila - Explore the stars and distant horizons. The uprated sensor suite and redesigned cockpit offer maximum visibility.

RSI Constellation Phoenix - A chariot of the gods, this converted luxury freighter is ideal for VIP transport.

RSI Constellation Taurus - Fully configurable but without all the bells-and-whistles, the Taurus is a great way to get started with crewed ships.

RSI Lynx - Tour the wildest corners of the ‘verse in safety, comfort, and style in the Lynx from RSI.

RSI Mantis - Stop ships dead in their tracks with RSI’s premier quantum enforcer.

RSI Meteor - A medium fighter providing a devastating mix of speed and firepower wrapped in the aggressive styling the brand is known for.

RSI Polaris - The Polaris is a nimble corvette-class capital ship that packs a powerful punch with a full armament of turrets and torpedoes.

RSI Scorpius - With an adaptable bi-wing configuration and revolutionary rail-mounted remote turret, the Scorpius offers unprecedented fire coverage, allowing for both defensive and assault-minded applications.

RSI Scorpius Antares - Redesigned to house a devastating EMP device and quantum jammer, the Antares shuts down enemy combatants, leaving them open to attack or boarding.

RSI Ursa - Rugged, durable, and tough, this is the rover of choice for extreme planetary exploration.

RSI Ursa Medivac - Provides frontline medical support essential to any ground operation.

RSI Zeus Mk II CL - With a focus on commerce, the Zeus Mk II CL features additional cargo space and a tractor beam for handling large volumes of freight.

RSI Zeus Mk II ES - With a focus on exploration, the Zeus Mk II ES features a robust radar package for making new discoveries along with enhanced weaponry and shielding.

Origin Jumpworks Day 2, November 21-22 Now that you've taken on some of the careers in the 'verse, why don't you get out there and explore a bit? Origin's lineup is perfect for checking out the clouds of Orison, the forests of microTech, or the canyons of Daymar. Here's what's available on Day 2:

Origin 85x - A luxury and sporty short-range runabout for pilot and passenger.

Origin 100i - Tour the universe with the perfect coupling of luxury and performance.

Origin 125a - With high fuel economy, a souped-up weapons package, and trademark Origin refinement, the 125a is the ideal entry into luxury spaceflight.

Origin 135c - With a deceptive amount of storage space in its sleek, stylish frame, the 135c is the obvious choice for the hauler of taste.

Origin 300i - Travel in style with this high-performance solo tourer.

Origin 315p - Traverse the ‘verse with this high-performance light explorer.

Origin 325a - Origin’s sleek signature fighter, the 325a makes a great companion for finding your mark in style and sophistication.

Origin 350r - Origin’s signature racer, the 350r leaves the competition in the dust.

Origin 400i - To explore the stars is a most noble endeavor, and Origin Jumpworks has risen to the occasion in crafting the 400i, the ultimate high-performance pathfinder.

Origin 600i Explorer - The 600i Explorer swaps the lounge for a robust scanning station as well as additional utility hardpoints to increase the ship's effectiveness.

Origin 600i Touring - Star Citizen’s iconic luxury tourer.

Origin 890 Jump - A vessel in a class all of its own, the colossal 890 Jump is a masterpiece of long-distance touring.

Origin M50 - Origin’s premier racer. Small, fast, and highly agile.

Origin X1 - The X1 takes speed and agility to the next level thanks to seamlessly integrated engine technology and joint vector thruster placement.

Origin X1 Force - This open-canopy vehicle from Origin is equally suited to ground-based exploration, reconnaissance expeditions, and security operations.

Origin X1 Velocity - The X1 Velocity offers a lighter chassis to improve overall performance, making it a dangerous new addition to the open-canopy racer lineup.

Drake Interplanetary Day 3, November 22-23 Ready to get your hands dirty? Whether through salvage with the Vulture, mining with the recent starter Golem, or tough combats with the Corsair, there’s potential for huge profits. Check out Drake’s vehicle lineup available on Day 3 below:

Drake Buccaneer - A light fighter that sacrifices durability (and its ejection seat!) for raw firepower.

Drake Caterpillar - A heavy multi-crew commercial freighter. Lightly armed with superior cargo capacity.

Drake Corsair - A worthy exploration companion, supporting you in battle, discovery, and delivery, wherever the winds of adventure may steer you.

Drake Cutlass Black - Back in black, Drake’s pirate-favorite is a highly versatile ship with combat and cargo prowess.

Drake Cutlass Blue - The Cutlass Blue boasts missiles, a more powerful engine, and Durasteel holding cells in the cargo bay.

Drake Cutlass Red - The Cutlass Red converts the standard cargo hold into a well-equipped medical facility, including two MedBeds.

Drake Cutlass Steel - Whoever has the guns and the personnel makes the rules. Drake has your back in both of those departments with the Cutlass Steel, featuring 18 jump seats and a wealth of firepower.

Drake Cutter - Designed for hard-working folks of all stripes, the Cutter packs 4 SCU of cargo room and plenty of wallop into a rough and tumble, compact frame.

Drake Cutter Rambler - The pilot-favorite Cutter chassis outfitted for long hauls and extended engagements. Go ahead, take the scenic route.

Drake Cutter Scout - The Scout model comes factory-equipped with a beefed-up scanning suite that makes it perfect for pathfinding, surveying, and even reconnaissance and covert intelligence operations.

Drake Dragonfly Black - A two-seater grav-lev bike that easily traverses rough terrain or open space.

Drake Golem - An accessible tool built to end the corporate monopoly on mining and place your future firmly within your grasp. Focused and highly capable yet accessible to all, it’s the ideal entry into deep-space mining.

Drake Herald - No secret is safe. Drake’s Herald captures and stores information before leaving at blistering speed.

Drake Mule - Whether you need to transport cargo over the roughest terrain possible or load it onto larger vessels and cargo decks, the Mule works, plain and simple.

Drake Vulture - Rip wrecks like a pro and carve out your own place in the great big empty behind the stick of this rough, rugged salvage machine from Drake Interplanetary.

Aopoa, Banu, Esperia, Gatac, Grey's Market Day 4, November 23-24 Craving a taste of alien technology and exotic designs? Visit IAE on Day 4:

AOPOA

Aopoa Khartu-al - Enigmatic, exotic, and agile. The fragile Khartu-al excels at lateral thrust and maneuverability.

Aopoa Nox - Sleek and fast, this gravity bike glides across rough terrain. Perfect for scouting and racing.

Aopoa San'tok.yāi - Meet the next evolution of Xi'an tech and design innovation. The San’tok.yāi is a fighter that literally flies circles around the competition.

BANU

Banu Defender - The exotic fighter is the first line of defense against enemy attack.

ESPERIA

Esperia Blade - This alien fighter slices through the air with high agility to shred foes to ribbons.

Esperia Glaive - This medium alien fighter replica drives fear with its impressive armament.

Esperia Prowler - The Prowler is a modernized version of the infamous Tevarin armored personnel carrier.

Esperia Prowler Utility - The Utility embraces the alien design of the infamous Tevarin ship entrusted to Esperia decades ago. However, its 32-SCU cargo hold and integrated tractor beam make this variant as practical for hauling as it is visually striking.

Esperia Stinger - A closely replicated Vanduul ship, reworked for Human flight. As Esperia’s first Heavy Fighter, the Stinger prioritizes strong armor to sustain prolonged barrages while readying its attack.

Esperia Talon - The Talon is the Tevarin equivalent to the Aegis Gladius or Vanduul Blade; a single-seat combat ship.

Esperia Talon Shrike - The infamous Shrike variant is armed with authentic internal missile racks capable of unleashing lethal barrages of projectiles.

GATAC MANUFACTURE

Gatac Syulen - The Syulen cargo vessel has been artfully crafted by the renowned House Gatac to perfectly suit both Human and Xi'an pilots.

GREY'S MARKET

Grey's Market Shiv - Don't ask how we got it, don't ask where it came from, just ask, "Do you want it?"

Kruger Intergalactic, MIRAI, MISC Day 5, November 24-25 Kruger's, Mirai and MISC's impressive lineups are available to try on Day 5:

KRUGER INTERGALACTIC

Kruger Wolf L-21 Wolf - A combat ship prioritizing quality and agility in a timeless design that encompasses Kruger Intergalactic’s core tenet - Perfection in Every Piece.

Kruger P-52 Merlin - Small, agile, and with a sting in its tail. This snub fighter is fragile but difficult to hit.

Kruger P-72 Archimedes - The Archimedes delivers exceptional handling and boost capabilities in a beautifully designed package.

MIRAI

Mirai Fury - Shatter the limits of performance with this next-generation snub fighter from Mirai featuring four halo-mounted size 2 laser repeaters, best-in-class maneuverability, and unprecedented integration of Xi’an tech.

Mirai Fury LX - The next-generation Fury LX racing ship from Mirai switches out the lithe ship’s offensive capabilities to make room for additional maneuvering thrusters perfect for getting across the finish line.

Mirai Fury MX - A ruthlessly efficient snub-bomber packing an intimidating payload that’s capable of delivering it with deadly precision.

Mirai Guardian - Single-operator, long-range heavy fighter with a focus on raw firepower and precision.

Mirai Guardian QI - Single-operator fighter-interceptor with a focus on raw firepower and precision.

Mirai Guardian MX - Mirai’s already deadly Guardian, tuned for uncompromised combat performance with harder-hitting weapons and heavier defense.

Mirai Pulse - Redefines the hoverbike experience with its fusion of sleek design, integrated weaponry, and advanced thrusters for unmatched maneuverability.

Mirai Pulse LX - The leader of high-speed thrills. Engineered to dominate, the LX strips away weight and cuts drag, thrusting you to the forefront of every race.

Mirai Razor - Cutting ahead of the competition, this sleek racer gives anyone a run for pole position.

Mirai Razor EX - Stealth-edition of the Razor outfitted with signature-reducing materials and low-draw components.

Mirai Razor LX - Special-edition of the Razor features reduced maneuverability and armament in exchange for extreme straight-line speed.

MUSASHI INDUSTRIAL AND STARFLIGHT CONCERN

MISC Fortune - Get the job done quickly with MISC’s most efficient salvager yet. It’s not a simple job, but the Fortune makes it easier.

MISC Freelancer - A multi-crew freighter with a turret and ordnance to deter those after its haul.

MISC Freelancer DUR - The Freelancer DUR specializes in exploration with improved scanner, jump drive, and fuel tanks.

MISC Freelancer MAX - The Freelancer MAX is for pilots who prize increased cargo capacity over everything else.

MISC Freelancer MIS - The Freelancer MIS is a limited-edition militarized variant of the classic merchant ship.

MISC Hull A - Where the others trade cargo capacity for firepower or speed, the Hull A is 100% on-mission transport.

MISC Hull C - Often called the most common ship in the galaxy, the Hull C cargo vessel is the most-produced of the range and is considered by many to be the most versatile.

MISC Prospector - A miner’s best friend, with a powerful laser and saddlebags to turn minerals to profit.

MISC Reliant Kore - A fusion of Xi’an and Human technology, this light freighter lets you haul cargo with a friend.

MISC Reliant Mako - Go where the news is and capture every moment with turret-mounted optics.

MISC Reliant Sen - The Reliant Sen is a versatile mobile science platform.

MISC Reliant Tana - An easy to maintain, versatile, lightweight fighter.

MISC Starfarer - The dedicated fuel refining platform from MISC.

MISC Starfarer Gemini - This military variant sacrifices fuel capacity for armor and a missile launcher.

MISC Starlancer MAX - Designed to carry huge payloads, the Starlancer MAX allows you to go big with a massively expansive cargo deck.

MISC Starlancer TAC - Heavy weaponry, a dedicated snub hangar, medbeds, and eight military-spec jump seats mean you’re ready for anything.

Anvil Aerospace Day 6, November 25-26 Looking for combat? Take the Mk2 Hornet for a spin. Prefer lending a helping hand instead? The Terrapin Medic is ideal for focusing on healing rather than fighting. You could also go on an adventure with your friends by renting an Asgard or a Paladin! Explore Anvil’s full lineup on Day 6 of IAE below:

Anvil Arrow - Featuring an ultra-aerodynamic frame and slight profile, it’s the most agile ship in its class.

Anvil Asgard - A heavily armored vehicle-dropship equipped for boundless resilience in the hottest combat zones. Power through relentless fire to deliver vital reinforcements, hold the front line, and keep the enemy retreating.

Anvil Ballista - This self-propelled air defense system is capable of destruction on a massive scale.

Anvil C8R Pisces - With the addition of an onboard Tier 3 Medical Bed, the C8R Pisces can treat minor injuries and keep a patient stable while transporting them to safety.

Anvil C8X Pisces Expedition - Ideal for inter-system travel or investigating tight spots inaccessible to larger ships, it’s a small ship ready for big adventures.

Anvil Carrack - Iconic multi-crew explorer ready for your next epic adventure.

Anvil Centurion - Built on Anvil’s popular Atlas Platform, the Centurion presents a tactical solution for short-range anti-aircraft engagement.

Anvil F7C Hornet Mk II - Tame the power, speed, and offensive punch of the UEE Navy's premier carrier-based fighter, made famous by its dominating role in the Vanduul war.

Anvil F7C-M Super Hornet Mk II - The Super Hornet is back and upgraded to Mk II spec, making it deadlier than ever. The only Hornet model with two seats, it features a dedicated gunner’s turret for increased firepower, accuracy, and all-round combat proficiency.

Anvil F7C-R Hornet Tracker Mk II - The F7CR “Tracker” model is a formidable stalker equipped with supercharged long-range radar.

Anvil F7C-S Hornet Ghost Mk II - The F7CS “Ghost” model is a stealth fighter more than capable of both reconnaissance and ambush operations.

Anvil F8C Lightning - A force to be reckoned with, it has protected Humanity countless times from countless threats at home and far from civilization.

Anvil Gladiator - A ruggedly built two-person dive bomber.

Anvil Hawk - The perfect ship for independent bounty hunters or local security.

Anvil Hurricane - A heavy fighter with an almost excessive loadout. Includes a turret that punches through shields and defenses.

Anvil Paladin - A formidable gunship with durable armor and immense firepower. Capable of hitting multiple targets simultaneously, the missiles, side turrets, and moveable central turret provide almost complete coverage as you lead the charge against enemies of the Empire.

Anvil Spartan - Ready for any battlefield, this vehicle gets troops there safely, quickly, and effectively.

Anvil Terrapin - Heavily armored ship with a sophisticated scanner. Ideal for recon and exploration.

Anvil Terrapin Medic - Sporting the same robust frame and armor as its pathfinding predecessor, the Terrapin Medic adds a Tier 2 MedBed to become a true miniature frontline trauma center or robust search and rescue vessel.

Anvil Valkyrie - A heavily armed dropship perfect for full-crew expeditions.

The Terrapin Medic is ideal for focusing on healing rather than fighting. You could also go on an adventure with your friends by renting an Asgard or a Paladin! ARGO Astronautics, Consolidated Outland, Greycat Industrial Day 7, November 26-27 Day 7 brings a wide array of manufacturers, offering plenty of gameplay choices. Whether you're into mining, delivery, hauling, or trying out power suits. Here’s the full lineup for Day 7:

ARGO ASTRONAUTICS

Argo ATLS - The ATLS power suit lets you tackle big jobs without the fuss of a vehicle. The specially designed exoframe uses a patented structural support system.

Argo ATLS GEO - Built on the proven ATLS power suit chassis, the GEO is outfitted with bespoke mining components and a Jump Pack to open up the most inaccessible (and prosperous) corners of the galaxy.

Argo CSV-SM - Rugged, reliable, and typically Argo, the CSV-SM gives you the power to move essential cargo anywhere, whatever the terrain.

Argo MOLE - Tap into your crew’s full potential with the combined force of Argo’s patented tri-lateral mining system.

Argo MPUV Cargo - A small, unarmed utility runabout designed for shuttling cargo.

Argo MPUV Personnel - A compact utility shuttle built for moving personnel.

Argo MPUV Tractor - The MPUV Tractor features dual tractor beams for effortless cargo handling alongside the sturdy, reliable design you expect from Argo.

Argo RAFT - Perfect for entry-level haulers and old pros alike, the RAFT is an ideal solution for reliable local freight transport.

Argo SRV - From simple freight and cargo towing to harrowing search-and-rescue operations, the SRV handles whatever you can throw at it.

CONSOLIDATED OUTLAND

CNOU HoverQuad - You know that place where the roads end, and sky runs out? That’s HoverQuad country, and it’s begging to be explored.

CNOU Mustang Alpha - Consolidated Outland’s premier ship for those wanting to push the limits a little further when starting out.

CNOU Mustang Beta - Home is where the heart is. The Beta offers comfortable living quarters for beginners roaming the frontier.

CNOU Mustang Gamma - An additional engine provides racers the competitive edge they need.

CNOU Mustang Delta - The Mustang Delta is armed with heavier weapons and rocket pods to give new pilots a little more firepower.

CNOU Nomad - The Nomad is ready to go anywhere and do anything - the perfect solution for anyone yearning to start a brand-new adventure.

GREYCAT INDUSTRIAL

Greycat MTC - The MTC is perfect for carrying weapons and armor to battlefields, bunkers, outposts, expedition sites, and more.

Greycat PTV - The Greycat PTV buggy gets you from point to point, wherever you are.

Greycat ROC - Designed to be as hard-working and versatile as the miners who use it.

Greycat ROC-DS - With more than double the ore capacity of the standard ROC, and a dedicated boom seat for manual laser operation, the ROC-DS makes big jobs manageable.

Greycat STV - A sports vehicle built by pros for pros that takes the industry-proven usability of Greycat and opens the door to adventure.

Crusader Industries, Tumbril Day 8, November 27-28 If you enjoy Orison’s clouds and its cherry blossom trees, then you’ll want to check out the manufacturer that calls the Crusader gas giant home: Crusader Industries! Check out the lineup from Crusader and Tumbril:

CRUSADER INDUSTRIES

Crusader A1 Spirit - A mid-size multi-purpose starship equipped as a light bomber but has the cargo and weaponry to deal with many different scenarios.

Crusader A2 Hercules - With more than double the firepower of the M2, and a custom bomb bay capable of delivering a staggering payload, the A2 caters to anyone hauling massive amounts of cargo through potentially unfriendly skies.

Crusader Ares Ion - This single cannon equipped heavy fighter delivers extremely powerful shots to quickly disable the shields of even the biggest enemy vessels.

Crusader Ares Inferno - Whether heading up a crew or hunting big ships solo, the Ares Inferno's massive Gatling tears through gunship armor and turns smaller fighters to dust in seconds.

Crusader C1 Spirit - A mid-size multi-purpose starship built for cargo transport and delivery but packing enough versatility to tackle multiple roles and unpredictable jobs.

Crusader C2 Hercules - Utilizing the patented Hercules military-grade spaceframe and expanding cargo capacity, while sacrificing barely any firepower, the C2 has become the cargo industry standard.

Crusader Intrepid - Versatile starter ship and light hauler built with true Crusader quality.

Crusader M2 Hercules - As the UEE's premier tactical Starlifter, the M2’s potent combination of capacity, maneuverability, and durability make it the obvious choice in large-scale transport.

Crusader Mercury Star Runner - Built with the same engineering and design principles that has made Crusader the go-to manufacturer for galactic transport on any scale, the Mercury checks all the boxes expected of a dependable courier vessel.

TUMBRIL LAND SYSTEMS

Tumbril Cyclone - Stir up a storm with this robust two-seater buggy that can carry a little something in the back.

Tumbril Cyclone AA - Features EMP functionality and an anti-air missile launcher to deter threats from above.

Tumbril Cyclone MT - Building on the agile off-road platform of the base variant, the MT adds two surface-to-air missile launchers and a ballistic cannon to keep airborne assailants at bay.

Tumbril Cyclone RC - Cyclone racing variant. It’s red, fast, and equipped with a built-in nitro booster.

Tumbril Cyclone RN - Built to clear the fog of war, the recon variant of the Cyclone features a powerful scanner array.

Tumbril Cyclone TR - Support infantry with this combat buggy. Equipped with a mounted turret to provide cover fire for ground operations.

Tumbril Nova - This heavy tank offers a devastating combination of weaponry to eliminate threats on the ground and in the air.

Tumbril Storm - The Tumbril Storm single-operator mini-tank is built to blitz battlefields and take out enemy artillery.

Tumbril Storm AA - Blitz overcrowded battlefields, take out threats from the air, and turn the tide of any conflict.

Grab an Aegis fighter and get your Bounty Hunting certification! Here's the full list available on Day 9:

Aegis Avenger Stalker - A modified version of the Avenger catering to bounty hunters thanks to built-in prison cells.

Aegis Avenger Titan - A former Advocacy patrol ship with added cargo capacity for light couriering.

Aegis Avenger Titan Renegade - Special-edition of the Avenger Titan with custom livery and a loadout geared to Arena Commander.

Aegis Avenger Warlock - A variant of the Avenger armed with an EMP generator to humanely disable enemies.

Aegis Eclipse - A sleek stealth bomber armed with heavy torpedoes.

Aegis Gladius - An aging but agile light-fighter boasting mid-range armament.

Aegis Gladius Valiant - Special-edition Gladius with custom livery and a loadout geared to Arena Commander.

Aegis Hammerhead - A multi-crew corvette bristling with manned turrets and heavy firepower.

Aegis Reclaimer - A vast deep-space salvage vessel built to reclaim wrecks and derelict ships.

Aegis Redeemer - Dotted with turrets and missiles, the Aegis Redeemer is a powerful fighting gunship capable of holding its own in combat with an impressive weapons payload.

Aegis Retaliator - One of Humanity’s most powerful warbirds, the Retaliator is a fearsome weapons platform originally designed to strike and kill capital ships.

Aegis Sabre - Favoring agility over durability, the Sabre is light, sleek, and deadly.

Aegis Sabre Comet - Special-edition of the Sabre with custom livery and a loadout geared to Arena Commander.

Aegis Sabre Firebird - Facilitating a devastating marriage of speed and ballistic firepower, the Firebird brings the heat to the infamous Sabre chassis.

Aegis Sabre Peregrine - The fastest Sabre model yet conceived, the Peregrine takes the infamous military-born chassis and tunes it for pure unadulterated speed.

Aegis Vanguard Harbinger - A powerful bomber that can operate out of the roughest forward-operating bases.

Aegis Vanguard Hoplite - Long-range squad dropship with a manned turret for protection.

Aegis Vanguard Sentinel - A ship designed to fight smart instead of taking enemies head-on.

Aegis Vanguard Warden - One of Aegis' most versatile and deadly long-range fighters. With an extra heavy frame, and an extra nasty loadout.

title: Traveler's Guide to the Galaxy: Nyx
summary: TRAVELER'S GUIDE TO THE GALAXY: NYX
body_html:
TRAVELER'S GUIDE TO THE GALAXY: NYX

Star System

Welcome to another edition of Traveler's Guide to the Galaxy. These dispatches aim to provide early insights into the lore and design shaping new locations coming to the Star Citizen universe. This time, we venture to Nyx, the third star system to join the 'verse, coming in Alpha 4.4*.

*In this edition, we'll be sharing a glimpse of what's on the horizon for Alpha 4.4, as well as a look further ahead at content planned for future updates. Please note that anything beyond Alpha 4.4 is subject to change as development continues.

Button The Glaciem Ring (or Nyx belt alpha) is a dense asteroid belt located between the second and third planets in the Nyx system.

WELCOME TO THE NYX SYSTEM

Nyx is an unclaimed planetary system situated at the border of a dark nebula. At its heart lies an F-type main sequence star, orbited by three planets and two sprawling asteroid belts.

As you travel towards the primary landing zone, your path will take you through the Glaciem Ring.

The belt is home to many old and decommissioned structures, like the Breaker Stations and more left behind by QV Planet Services.

For years, miners from throughout the 'verse traveled to the ring to make their fortunes.

The largest object in the belt is called Delamar, an enormous asteroid and home to the famous mining facility, Levski.

LEVSKI

Settlement

The system's primary settlement, Levski, is built into a large asteroid within the Glaciem Ring. Once a mining facility, Levski has evolved into a refuge for those seeking life beyond the tightening grip of the United Empire of Earth (UEE). Today, it stands as a symbol of independence and resistance; a place where ideals of freedom and self-governance endure.

Tucked away on the rugged terrain of Delamar lies Levski, a fascinating independent settlement with a story as bold as its founders. This off-the-grid haven was established in SEY 2655 within the bones of a long-abandoned QV Planet Services mining facility.

Named after a 19th-century Earth revolutionary, Levski was founded by the People's Alliance, a group of political dissenters who envisioned a society free from tyranny. During the oppressive Messer Era, the settlement became a beacon for refugees fleeing Earth (Sol III) and a sanctuary for those escaping unjust government persecution.

Pirates, smugglers, and outlaws have all passed through its corridors.

While Levski prides itself on its egalitarian ideals, its remote location and anti-establishment roots have also made it a magnet for less savory visitors...

Despite this, the People's Alliance continues to stand firm, defending their vision of freedom and community.

THE TANAKA MEMORIAL

The entrance of Levski is dominated by a statue of an unnamed worker holding the lifeless body of Anthony Tanaka, a child laborer who was executed by an Advocacy agent in 2757 for refusing to continue work after a 16-hour shift at a munitions factory. Footage of the murder was smuggled out of the factory, and became a symbol of resistance to the growing members of the anti-Messer movement. The Tanaka Memorial stands as a solemn reminder to the People's Alliance to never return to the UEE.

Each year on December 3rd, Anthony Tanaka Remembrance Day honors the child whose act of defiance became a rallying cry across the empire.

Mercy Hospital, Levski's primary medical hub, offers emergency care and advanced treatment to travelers and locals alike.

Find everything from everyday supplies to rare and exotic goods at the Grand Barter. Haggling is expected, and the atmosphere is as much a draw as the wares. The bazaar is also home to the iconic Café Musain.

THE PEOPLE'S ALLIANCE

STRONGER TOGETHER

A faction originally formed by people fleeing the unjust Messer regime, they founded a utopian colony in a ready-made station on an asteroid in the Nyx system. In spite of the challenges of living on an airless rock, their settlement, Levski, endures to this day. The People’s Alliance of Levski are dedicated to the creation and continual development of a truly egalitarian community, where all may feel safe and free to express ideas while supporting each other towards the communal goal of enlightened self-sufficiency. However, there are those who seek to take advantage the People's Alliance's lofty goals for their own selfish gain...

A TASTE OF DELAMAR

NOTABLY NYX'S

Remote, rugged, and rich in character, Delamar has quietly become a source of some of the most distinctive drinks in the UEE. Whether brewed in cave stills or whispered about in cocktail lore, its contributions are worth a toast.

TRISE SLING

While Trise Cordial isn't native to Nyx, its most famous cocktail may well be. The Trise Sling, a whiskey-based drink that gained popularity at G-Loc Bar in Area18, is said to have originated on Delamar.

Local bartender Clair Rios of Café Musain claims she created the recipe in 2911, only for it to be "borrowed" by G-Loc staff passing through Nyx. Whether stolen or simply shared, the Sling has become a staple across the UEE, but in Delamar, it's still considered a homegrown classic.

JYNX GIN

Distilled and bottled on Delamar, Jynx Gin owes its striking coloration and part of its mystique to the omphalotus mushroom. First brewed in 2901 by bartender and local legend Alta Turei, Jynx began as an experiment to craft a drink using ingredients native to Delamar's harsh terrain. After many failed attempts, Turei's breakthrough came with the omphalotus, resulting in a gin that glows faintly pink and tastes like rebellion in a bottle.

Today, from quiet lounges to bustling spaceports, Jynx Gin is a go-to for bartenders looking to serve something with flair and story.

A GLIMPSE AHEAD

Beyond Alpha 4.4

What follows is a preview of content that's planned for future updates and not included in Alpha 4.4. They reflect longer-term development goals and may change as work progresses.

LOCATIONS

New locations will arrive with future content drops. Here's a look at what's coming into play further down the line.

BREAKER STATIONS

MUNICIPAL WORKS

TACTICAL STRIKE GROUPS

PLANETS

NYX I

A green yet uninhabitable world undergoing an experimental terraformation process, Nyx I may soon have an atmosphere that will let everyone breathe free. While their quality of life would improve substantially if they relocated to an inhabitable planet, some members of the People's Alliance are worried that access to an abundance of resources will undermine their collectivist values.

NYX II

The air on Nyx II is sweltering, stifling, and extremely poisonous. A smog planet located in the system's green band, it has been impossible to terraform due to technological limitations. However, the unpleasant nature of the world does have one benefit: there may still be an untapped wealth of resources waiting for those brave and industrious enough to claim for their own.

NYX III

Furthest planet from the star at the center of the Nyx system, Nyx III is an ice giant with a stormy atmosphere.

10/20/2025 - 11:00 PM This Week in Star Citizen Hello everyone, xē'suelen nyahyan

Last week welcomed Alpha 4.3.2: Fractured Frontiers to the Live servers. This update introduces the mysterious Yormandi encounter, improvements to Structural Salvage and the FPS Tractor Beam, three new ships: the Stinger, Paladin, and Shiv. You will also find new weapons, quality-of-life updates, plenty of bug fixes, and the start of Phase 1 of the Frontier Fighters Finale, concluding the Pyro Must Burn storyline. Read the full Patch Notes and join the initial reconnaissance efforts.

The Day of the Vara 2955 celebration continues across Stanton and beyond, featuring two community contests: pumpkin decorating and horror stories. Players can also earn a Spectrum badge, take on the limited-time Kill Collector mode in Arena Commander to unlock eerie Halloween masks, and enjoy themed ship paints and other festivities through November 3. There’s still time to show off your creativity and claim a spooky reward!

Our teams are also collecting your feedback on Alpha 4.3.2 while preparing for upcoming events and the release of Alpha 4.4.0, which is expected to reach Evocati soon!

Now, let's see what's going on this week:

On Wednesday, the Roadmap Update and Roundup will be a follow-up to the recent announcements made during CitizenCon Direct 2955, along with additional 4.4.0 cards to the Release View, to prepare for the content ahead!

Also on Wednesday, our servers will be offline for approximately four hours starting at 12:00 p.m. UTC. During this maintenance window, all gameplay systems will be unavailable, and you will not be able to access the game until maintenance is complete. We will provide updates on the RSI Status Page as progress continues.

This downtime will allow us to implement several tweaks to the Live build, including fixes for commodities that would not sell at TDD locations, issues preventing datapad pickups, an update to Wikelo’s Emporium featuring the new Mission Pickup on Location feature, and a few other improvements.

On Friday, be sure to check your inbox for the RSI Weekly Newsletter. We will recap the week's highlights, showcase standout community content, and provide a sneak peek at what's coming next. Don't forget to subscribe to the Newsletter in your account's settings.

title: Roadmap Roundup - October 22, 2025
summary: 10/22/2025 - 9:00 PM Roadmap Roundup Hello everyone!
body_html:
10/22/2025 - 9:00 PM Roadmap Roundup Hello everyone!

Every two weeks, we accompany the Roadmap update with a brief explanatory note to give you insight into the decision-making that led to any changes. This is part of an effort to make our communications more transparent, more specific, and more insightful for all of you who help to make Star Citizen and Squadron 42 possible.

Just a reminder: The 1.0 column showcases features and content planned for inclusion in or before Star Citizen 1.0. This means you may not have to wait for the 1.0 release to experience them. As features/content in the 1.0 column become ready, they will migrate left into a point patch column for release.

Be sure to check back every two weeks for the latest updates.

With that, let’s dive into this week’s Roadmap Roundup!

-CIG Community Team

Notable Changes: October 22, 2025

Release View

4.3.2

All 4.3.2 cards were marked as Released. Some notable additions:

Assault Rifle "Killshot"

Featuring both a ballistic and energy projectile, this rifle fires each in tandem giving you the best of both worlds with a competitive magazine size, high damage and a punchy aim profile.

This card has been set to Released.

LMG "Pulverizer"

This LMG features a massive drum mag firing 50.cal rounds down range at targets, hitting as hard as it looks with a low RPM and deadly damage. It uses the same profile as the recent VOLT LMG, allowing you to fire at targets from longer distances.

This card has been set to Released.

Blade "VCK-1"

These Vanduul-inspired knives are a new melee weapon using the classic melee mechanics, but with a deadly alien twist.

This card has been set to Released.

Anvil Paladin

Introducing Anvil Aerospace’s latest gunship: the Paladin.

This card has been set to Released.

Esperia Stinger

Implementing Esperia's latest Vanduul replica, the Heavy Fighter Stinger.

This card has been set to Released.

Grey's Market Shiv

Implementing Grey's Market's first ship to the 'verse: the Shiv.

This card has been set to Released.

Mission Pickup on Location

Enabling new missions to be discovered and added to journals when you approach or enter a designated area. This is first being introduced to Wikelo's Imperium.

This card has been set to Released.

Monocular Range Finders

The Monocular Range Finders make surveying the battlefield easier, with a 10x zoom to spot hostiles at distance and light amplification providing greater night visibility.

This card has been set to Released.

4.4.0

New Wikelo Ships Offerings (4.4.0)

Adding multiple new vehicles and equipment to the ever-expanding Wikelo's Emporium: RSI Meteor and the Guardian MX, with upgraded components and a unique base livery. These rewards can be unlocked by completing Wikelo's contracts.

This card has been set to Tentative.

Shotgun Pistol "TripleDown"

Bolt action, mag drum, triple barrel and a buckshot pistol.

This card has been set to Tentative.

Missile Launcher "Boomtube"

Three rockets strapped together in a tube releasing a single deadly payload. This weapon has high spread and an arming distance leaning into its chaotic unpredictable nature of finding the sweet spot distance.

This card has been set to Tentative.

Interstellar Hauling Missions

Implementing hauling missions that start in one system and finish in another.

This card has been set to Tentative.

Exterior Freight Elevators

Adding new ways of loading and unloading cargo in Nyx and Pyro.

This card has been set to Tentative.

Nyx Missions (Pack 1)

Adding a first pack of missions to Nyx, using existing archetypes with a fresh new narrative spin against new enemies.

This card has been set to Tentative.

Nyx Jump Points

Introducing jump points between Nyx and Pyro, and between Nyx and Stanton.

This card has been set to Tentative.

Vanduul NPC Pilots

The Stinger, Glaive, Scythe, and Blade make an appearance as NPC ships flown by Vanduul.

This card has been set to Tentative.

Sworn Enemies

Implementing a new operation welcoming players to Nyx. InterSec is looking for contractors willing to investigate abandoned QV Logistics stations to follow the trail of Vanduul tech that was sold to ASD.

This card has been set to Tentative.

Nyx System

Implementing the Nyx star system into the persistent universe.

This card has been set to Tentative.

Glaciem Ring

Implementing the Glaciem Ring, a dense asteroid belt located in the Nyx system.

This card has been set to Tentative.

Delamar

Implementing Delamar, an inhabited asteroid in the Nyx system, home to the settlement of Levski.

This card has been set to Tentative.

Levski

Implementing Levski, a settlement on the asteroid Delamar in the Nyx system.

This card has been set to Tentative.

QV Services Stations

Implementing abandoned QV Stations across Nyx, some now occupied by a new enemy faction.

This card has been set to Tentative.

Medium Battle Tech Armor

Adding a new Medium Battle Tech Armor.

This card has been set to Tentative.

Wikelo Medium Battle Tech Armor

Adding a new Wikelo Medium Battle Tech Armor that players can obtain by completing the corresponding mission from Wikelo's Emporium.

This card has been set to Tentative.

New Hairstyles (4.4.0)

Adding one additional hairstyle, and eleven new facial hair customization for your character.

This card has been set to Tentative.

Join the discussion on Spectrum.

10/13/2025 - 9:00 PM This Week in Star Citizen Happy post-CitizenCon Direct, everyone!

This year’s big event may have been beamed digitally, but it didn’t stop the excitement from spreading far and wide. Across North America and Europe, members of our team joined nine simultaneous CitizenCon Direct 2955 Watch Parties, sharing reactions, cheering on the reveals, and celebrating the 'verse that many of us call a home away from home. The members of our team who were fortunate enough to attend in person and share the day with you were met with a vivid reminder of the energy, creativity, and dedication that make this community truly one of a kind. CitizenCon Direct gave us a glimpse of what’s coming, sooner than you'd expect. Get ready to welcome Nyx, our third star system (and the second to be released in the same calendar year!), in an upcoming PTU patch on the horizon — stay tuned!

title: Q&A: Paladin & Stinger
summary: Q&A: Anvil Paladin & Esperia Stinger
body_html:
Q&A: Anvil Paladin & Esperia Stinger

As revealed during CitizenCon Direct 2955, the Anvil Paladin and Esperia Stinger are making their debut as flyable ships with the Alpha 4.3.2 patch. The Paladin is a dedicated gunship built for frontline combat, while the Stinger is Esperia’s faithful replica of a deadly Vanduul heavy fighter. We caught up with the Vehicle and Gameplay teams to learn more about these two new ships. Here are the answers, straight from the devs themselves.

Q&A: Anvil Paladin & Esperia StingerAs revealed during CitizenCon Direct 2955, the Anvil Paladin and Esperia Stinger are making their debut as flyable ships with the Alpha 4.3.2 patch. The Paladin is a dedicated gunship built for frontline combat, while the Stinger is Esperia’s faithful replica of a deadly Vanduul heavy fighter. We caught up with the Vehicle and Gameplay teams to learn more about these two new ships. Here are the answers, straight from the devs themselves. Anvil Paladin

Anvil Paladin The Anvil Paladin is a gunship truly deserving of its moniker. This flying stronghold delivers immense multi-turreted firepower alongside heavy armor for sustained barrage and ultimate fortification, as you lead your fleet into new systems and beyond.

Since the original concept reveal, have there been any notable changes or additions to the Paladin? The main noticeable change to the Paladin has been the adjustment of the lower deck to accommodate a dedicated 4-SCU cargo grid.

How does the Paladin differ from existing gunships? The Paladin’s primary competitor is the Redeemer, but they tackle the gunship role in different ways. The Paladin favors firepower and durability over the more agile Redeemer that, while packing slightly less firepower, has the edge in avoiding incoming fire.

Is the Paladin intended to shine more in coordinated group play, or can it still be effective for smaller crews? Whether being flown solo or in a group, the Paladin is capable of delivering firepower to where it’s needed. A solo player has slaved control of the two remote wing turrets, providing firepower in the forward arc, but this is improved with additional players taking control of the turrets to provide full 360° coverage.

What interior features does the Paladin provide for its crew? The lower deck houses an armory equipped with suit lockers and weapon racks, while the upper deck provides crew amenities including a food machine, toilet, bunk beds, and personal storage.

Esperia Stinger

Esperia Stinger The Esperia Stinger is a heavy fighter where durability and deadly force combine in this closely replicated Vanduul powerhouse. Fortified armor and robust wings withstand damage, while a customizable loadout of Human and Vanduul weaponry delivers it.

Aside from its aggressive appearance, what characteristics distinguish the Stinger from Human ships? The Stinger is a relatively faithful recreation of the original Vanduul Stinger, so while externally and internally you will see a very strong alien aesthetic, there are touches that Esperia added for Human comfort, such as the weapon rack and relay access.

Does it come equipped with alien-style weapons, and which of its gun and missile components are bespoke versus swappable? Six of the seven guns found on the Stinger are generic swappable weapons, coming with Esperia laser cannons. Only the single Size 5 weapon is bespoke and locked to the ship. The missile racks, whilst bespoke, allow the missiles to be swapped with any other suitable S2 missile.

How does the Stinger compare in handling and firepower to Human-designed Heavy Fighters, such as the Ares, F8C Lightning, or Guardian? Due to the sheer size and firepower of the Stinger, its handling feels much heavier than the Human-designed Heavy Fighters at this time. As such, it’s suited to taking on other Heavy Fighters and larger targets.

Will the Stinger feature an updated MFD UI? Yes! The Stinger has an updated Esperia MFD style incorporating typefaces and graphical elements from the Vanduul language.

With the release of the Stinger, are there any updates planned for the other Vanduul replicas, such as the Blade and Glaive? We still plan to bring these over to the PU once Squadron 42 has been released.

title: This Week in Star Citizen
summary: 10/06/2025 - 7:30 PM This Week in Star Citizen Hello everyone, xē'suelen nyahyan
body_html:
10/06/2025 - 7:30 PM This Week in Star Citizen Hello everyone, xē'suelen nyahyan

Last week brought the PU Monthly Report, offering an in-depth look at September’s development progress across our teams, while Day of the Vara 2955 ushered Halloween into the ‘verse.

The celebration of Day of the Vara 2955 continues with spooky vibes across Stanton and beyond, featuring two community contests (pumpkin decorating and horror stories), an earnable Spectrum badge, the return of the limited-time FPS Kill Collector mode in Arena Commander that unlocks eerie Halloween masks, themed ship paints, and plenty of fun running through November 3.

Meanwhile, the Alpha 4.3.2 PTU cycle is now open to all waves, introducing new stories to experience, mysteries to unravel, and a host of quality-of-life improvements. Check the regularly updated PTU Patch Notes for the latest changes, and share your feedback on the Frontier Fighters finale event, FPS Beam Tractor improvements, Structural Salvage updates, and other new features currently in testing.

Now, let's see what's going on this week:

On Tuesday, the Subscriber Comm-Link and Newsletter launch the month with exclusive perks and fresh flair for our subscribers.

On Wednesday, the Roadmap Update and Roundup will provide a follow-up on Alpha 4.3.2, which is currently available to all waves in the PTU environment.

On Friday, be sure to check your inbox for the RSI Weekly Newsletter. We will recap the week's highlights, showcase standout community content, and provide a sneak peek at what's coming next. Don't forget to subscribe to the Newsletter in your account's settings.

And finally on Saturday, it's time for CitizenCon Direct 2955! Tune in at 1900 UTC for a ~two-hours broadcast live on Twitch and YouTube. We're also heading out to nine Bar Citizen Watch Parties across North America and Europe to celebrate with the community in person. Whether you're a veteran pilot or just beginning your journey, join us to connect with fellow Citizens, share stories, and experience the excitement together. Whether you're at home, or at a Watch Party, we'll see you there!

a.thl'ē'kol, see you soon,

title: Roadmap Roundup - October 8, 2025
summary: 10/08/2025 - 10:30 PM Roadmap Roundup Hello everyone!
body_html:
10/08/2025 - 10:30 PM Roadmap Roundup Hello everyone!

Every two weeks, we accompany the Roadmap update with a brief explanatory note to give you insight into the decision-making that led to any changes. This is part of an effort to make our communications more transparent, more specific, and more insightful for all of you who help to make Star Citizen and Squadron 42 possible.

Just a reminder: The 1.0 column showcases features and content planned for inclusion in or before Star Citizen 1.0. This means you may not have to wait for the 1.0 release to experience them. As features/content in the 1.0 column become ready, they will migrate left into a point patch column for release.

Be sure to check back every two weeks for the latest updates.

With that, let’s dive into this week’s Roadmap Roundup!

-CIG Community Team

Notable Changes: October 8, 2025

Release View

4.3.2

Structural Salvage

Additional balancing of structural salvage as part of ongoing refining changes related to upcoming work on crafting.

This card has been set to Tentative.

Klaus & Werner Laser Repeater Art Refactors

Updating several Klaus & Werner Laser Repeaters' art style and geometry: Size 1, 2, and 3.

This card's visual has been updated.

New Wikelo Ships Offerings (4.3.2)

Adding multiple new ships, equipment, and vehicles to the ever-expanding Wikelo's Emporium: Crusader A2 Hercules, Crusader Ares Starfighter Inferno and Ion, Esperia Prowler Utility, with upgraded components and a unique base livery. These rewards can be unlocked by completing Wikelo's contracts.

This card's visual has been updated.

AI FPS Turret

Adding anti-personnel turrets for players to avoid or destroy, providing additional PvE challenges.

This card's visual has been updated.

Heavy Battle Tech Armor "Palatino"

Adding a new Heavy Battle Tech Armor.

This card's name has been updated.

Frontier Fighters Finale

A new event in 4.3.2 related to the Fight for Pyro storyline.

This card's name has been updated.

Mission Pickup on Location

Enabling new missions to be discovered and added to journals when you approach or enter a designated area.

This card has been set to Tentative.

Yormandi

A large creature introduced in Alpha 4.3.2, the Yormandi lurks in the depths of the Onyx Facilities.

This card has been set to Tentative.

Yormandi Cave

Deep within Site-B at the Onyx Facilities lies the hidden lair of the Yormandi, waiting to be uncovered.

title: Star Citizen Monthly Report: September 2025
summary: PU Monthly Report September 2025 With Alpha 4.3.1: Virtue's Descent live and another thrilling update this month, the Star Citizen universe has never been more packed with adventure. Read on for everything done at CIG’s studios throughout September in pursuit of this new content, from updated backend code to all-new missions and more.
body_html:
PU Monthly Report September 2025 With Alpha 4.3.1: Virtue's Descent live and another thrilling update this month, the Star Citizen universe has never been more packed with adventure. Read on for everything done at CIG’s studios throughout September in pursuit of this new content, from updated backend code to all-new missions and more.

AI Content

The AI Content team continued to test updates to some of the landing-zone NPCs, looping in the QA team to help stress test the setup to ensure it can take the strain of extensive use and trigger any potential issues.

To make stations and cities feel more alive, the team leveraged the med-station behavior used during the regen crisis. Now, shopkeepers will interact more with the people frequenting their store. The team is also looking at an underutilized aspect of landing-zone archetypes and are preparing a proposal to make better use of guards.

In addition to the ongoing task of setting up comms-call characters for missions, the devs also started looking at mission providers in general and built a new behavior to support face-to-face interactions in the future.

AI (Features)

AI Features updated numerous features last month, beginning with AIWeaponComponent, which will now remain in sync with weapon statuses, allowing them to work better in unison.

Support was then added for NPCs to systematically target vehicles in combat. Improvements were made to the ‘rocketeer’ behavior, allowing NPCs to switch between using a rocket launcher and pistol depending on the situation. Adjustments to the visuals of various behaviors were made, improving cover usage and fixing multiple asserts.

Default behaviors were then introduced to the Buddy AI, allowing NPCs to follow their leader and stay in close proximity during combat. ‘TPS Covers Along Path’ was finalized based on feedback, while ammo-looting updates are underway too. This will affect holstering and stowing primary weapons and prevent NPCs from switching to their pistols when looting if they still have primary-weapon ammo.

Formerly mentioned in previous Monthly Reports as an upcoming creature, the new Yormandi now uses different fire modes in its attacks. Issues with perception giving false positives were also fixed. Further improvements are currently underway for this and existing creatures.

In addition, new functionality was added for testing first reactions by generating test-cell level variants, making rapid iteration and testing easier for each situation. This includes testing for first reactions and animation flows.

AI (Tech)

September saw AI Tech improve NPCs using elevators by simplifying the set up of the transit carriage. Focus is currently on 3D navigation and NPCs flying ships.

The team continued to improve the flight-path finder system and 3D collision avoidance using the newer voxel-grid approach for custom environments. The focus is to unify the process flow with the one used for ground requests and pre-emptive adaptation of the pathfinder structure. This will deal with the paths generated if a spatial voxel grid is present. This also includes the introduction of distinct parallel jobs for search and refinement, and how the flight path is constructed. Additionally, hard turns have been introduced alongside allowing ships to get ‘nose on target’ more quickly.

Development was done on AI perception code, with the team fixing issues with knowledge escalation when seeing enemies between the primary and secondary fields of view.

Direct perception was also introduced, which simulates knowledge at distance. For example, when NPCs communicate via comms. This enables systemic reactions to NPCs being killed while talking, even without direct line of sight.

Improvements were then made to the way assignments are queued in relation to the usable builder tool. Crashes during general use were also fixed, such as when changing alignment slots and expanding the line popup edit for geom and helper geom editing.

Updates were made to the AI sequence system, which manages AI agent scripting in the flowgraph. This enforces the validation of action sequences and ensures the correct execution context is set in the systemic activities, providing a more reliable way to manually script agents and to guarantee actions are validated and executed correctly.

The critical flow mode for AI agents was brushed up too. While in this mode, action-execution errors are still reported but can now be handled with specific fallback, allowing the flow to proceed instead of failing and potentially stalling. This is still in progress and will be further enhanced going forward.

StarScript improvements are still being made as the team improve the tool following feedback from the devs. Finally, Subsumption content data improvements were made to reduce errors going forward.

AI (Game Intelligence Development Team)

In September, the Game Intelligence Development team focused on completing the next milestone for Mission System 2.0. They’re currently breaking down the work and discussing the best possible path to approach the implementation.

They also continued to fix bugs and performance issues, and worked on features suggested by the designers to improve StarScript.

Animation

The Animation team continued to work on an upcoming creature and ‘boss’ fight alongside supporting a new mission giver.

Facial Animation progressed through new performances that were captured in late August. These include characters that will be present in multiple upcoming releases, including a returning air-traffic control voice.

The Animation, Narrative, and Mo-cap teams also planned for their next shoot, which will be held at the beginning of October.

Art (Characters)

The Character Art team finalized both new armors and a new gang. Work also continued on polishing the Yormandi.

The Concept Art team continued iterating on new armors.

Art (Ships)

In the UK, work continued to bring the RSI Aurora and Aegis Hammerhead up to modern standard. The Aurora progressed through the LOD0 and Final stages as improvements were made to the component bays, bed access, dashboard placement, entrance method, VTOL setup, and cargo access on the underside.

For the Hammerhead, focus was on implementing the improvements made to the base corridor kit from the recent Idris release, alongside making sure the component bays and relays are suitably placed and accessible.

The Paladin progressed into the LOD0 phase, with final adjustments being made to the main quad turret to ensure its movement is unhindered in both flight and landed states. The downstream teams kicked off their work on the ship too.

The MISC Hull B is now well into the whitebox phase. The majority of the interior was implemented to the required level, while adjustments are currently being made to the exterior mesh to meet the gate requirements.

Following last month’s work, the Drake Ironclad and Ironclad Assault (plus the updated Command Module) are approaching their combined whitebox gate review.

Four unannounced vehicles also continued development throughout September. The first is approaching its LOD0 review, while the second progressed through the LOD0 gate and is now in its final stage.

The third, a variant of a popular recent release, is receiving greybox and LOD0 work in tandem due to the nature of the changes. The fourth passed its greybox review early in September, with the LOD0 work due early October. Some of the downstream teams began their tasks too.

The North American teams began the month finalizing fixes for the RSI Apollo ships ahead of their release. Various optimizations were also made following player use in the PTU.

LOD0 for the RSI Perseus was also passed early on in the month, with the team moving onto the final touches and downstream teams beginning to close out the ship.

The whitebox phase officially kicked off for the Drake Kraken in the latter half of the month. Last month’s preproduction phase led to numerous improvements and adjustments to navigation, flow, and interactions throughout the ship.

Two unannounced vehicles progressed too. One moved through the greybox phase, while the second entered whitebox.

Community

The team kicked off the month with the grand finale of this year’s Ship Showdown, where the RSI Polaris claimed the crown. To honor the champion, all backers will receive an in-game commemorative Polaris-themed holographic banner at this year’s Intergalactic Aerospace Expo (IAE). The Anvil Asgard, Anvil Gladiator, and RSI Zeus MK II ES rounded out the top four - all four will receive new 2955 Best in Show paints and posters at IAE.

Ship Showdown was not the only race to reach its conclusion. The Race for Stanton also crowned its champion, with Hurston Dynamics amassing a staggering 337,131,104 SCU to secure victory, followed by microTech, Crusader, and ArcCorp.

Pirate Week sailed into port as crew and corsairs proudly flew their colors in the Pirate Flag Design Contest. The team charted the course for the Treasure Hunt by crafting riddles and clues that sent players searching across Stanton and Pyro, while each This Week in Star Citizen during the event spotlighted a pirate organization.

To support the release of Alpha 4.3.1: Virtue’s Descent, the team published a catch-all post, updated the Onyx Facilities FAQ, and released a dedicated Q&A for the newly flyable RSI Apollo. They also worked closely with internal teams to track sentiment and community feedback, ensuring community notes landed in the right developer hands.

The team also continued their evergreen tasks, which included publishing This Week in Star Citizen, bi-weekly Roadmap Updates and Roundups, and other updates, such as Monthly Reports like this one. They also gathered pressing questions from the community, followed up with developers, and assembled Comms-Dive #3, which provided detailed answers on topics ranging from ship lights to upcoming UI improvements.

The Bar Citizen World Tour made two exciting stops in Lisbon, Portugal, and Rome, Italy.

“We had an incredible time connecting with the community in Portugal and Italy, both of which hosted incredible events!” Community Team

Finally, CitizenCon Direct 2955 is almost here. The team is working closely with community organizers on several CitizenCon Direct Watch Parties, with key members of CIG attending events across North America and Europe. Be sure to check the locations to join the celebration.

Core Gameplay

As part of ongoing medical gameplay improvements, the team provided support for bespoke ‘take’ and ‘place’ animations, and reworked the implementation of players clearing their respawn point in vehicles. Bug fixes were implemented for the medical screen, along with improved validation to make it easier to spot errors.

Tiered medical bed spawn ranges were reimplemented for more robust compatibility with Server Meshing. Additionally, new controls were exposed to the designers that allow them to control healing cost per medical bed tier, while additional data was exposed to the UI designers to add new information to the medical screens.

For engineering, the team continued iterating on playtest feedback and hardening the feature ahead of wider-scale testing.

The Vehicle Command Module feature continued through its pre-production phase, with the devs completing the prototype and technical design. Additional debug tooling revealed various issues with the underlying docking system, prompting an effort to fix critical flow issues.

Flight gameplay also progressed throughout September. AI can now correctly utilize Control Surfaces in-atmosphere and adhere to their velocity goals. Annunciators are no longer required to be attached to a dashboard to be functional, allowing for more flexibility in cockpit design. The team also prepared for focus testing of the improved flight model.

The ongoing inventory rework progressed with the implementation of equipment and equipped-item slots. Further functionality was added to the paperdoll UI and search bar. The team also exposed controls to help Design define the rules for proximity looting.

Economy

The Economy team began the month exploring how to make the players’ impact on freelancing commodity trading more impactful and longer lasting. In the process, they adjusted offer and demand at some locations while tuning profits to fit the current level of the economy.

The team then evaluated the data on the drop rates of some rare items and made them more prevalent.

The cargo manifests found in spawned ships were also redesigned so their value doesn’t undermine the intended gameplay for certain missions.

Mission Design

Mission Design began September finalizing the last narrative mission for the ASD facilities before looking forward to the rest of the year’s content. They also began removing old factions players will no longer work with and reorganizing the ones they will.

Alongside this, the team reviewed bounty missions and added comms notifications for the mission provider. This is part of the ongoing initiative to bring older missions up to standard.

Mission Design also worked alongside Engineering to solve long-standing issues with spawn closets and made more fixes to the mission-generation systems.

Narrative

In September, the Narrative team focused on tasks to help close out the rest of the year strongly. They focused on crafting scripts that will add additional dynamic conversations, a new Covalex mission representative, vendors, and customers to the game, and spent time generating mission text and lore discoverables for several upcoming events.

Narrative then worked alongside with the Environment Art and Branding teams on the signage and environmental storytelling for several incoming levels.

Time was also spent planning narrative initiatives for the next year. This was an excellent opportunity to learn from the recent releases and continue to strengthen the players' narrative experiences across the game.

Online Technology

Last month, the Live Tools team updated the error reporting pipeline, including moving panic migration from Heap to Laravel. The panic webapp tool can now configure stream settings, removing dev time by allowing users to define the configuration of each stream themselves. The symbolizer was also rewritten to be event-driven, making it more stable and scalable.

Progress was made on a new webapp to configure Bootstrap settings, which will provide a more accessible display for its users.

For Hex, implementation began of the audit-log UI that will extend the system’s filtering and sorting capabilities. Concepting for Hex 4.0 continued too.

The Online Services team continued to work on item recovery and the blueprint service, alongside continued bugfixing and support.

R&D

In September, the R&D team’s focus remained exclusively on analyzing performance and optimizing engine and game code.

VFX

For Alpha 4.3.2, VFX finished up their tasks for the ASD locations and final event work, while the RSI Apollo Triage and Medivac received their VFX passes. Production continued on the Yormandi and its related locations too.

VFX passes also began for vehicles coming later in the year alongside pre-production for upcoming locations and missions starting in the next week or so.

With expertise in mold design and advanced manufacturing, they bring exceptional detail and authenticity to every creation. As a licensed partner, PLANET-RING showcased the F8C Lightning, Gladius, and Hammerhead prototypes at CitizenCon 2024, highlighting their dedication to precision and craftsmanship. Their debut release, the 1:100 scale F8C Lightning plastic-injection model, launches in 2026 as both a plastic model kit and a pre-built display piece featuring dynamic LED lighting. Both models are available to pre-order now, marking the beginning of an ongoing collection that brings the universe of Star Citizen from the 'verse to your shelf.

Known for large-scale creations, such as the UEES Retribution and Port Olisar, Pigeon Spaceport continues to deliver exceptional craftsmanship and detail for collectors across the ‘verse. Their 1:100 scale RSI Scorpius model is now available for pre-order, offering a pre-assembled and pre-painted collectible built from precision-injected ABS. Movable engines and wings allow seamless transitions between takeoff and landing configurations, supported by a sturdy metal base for display and a custom wooden case for protection. Pigeon Spaceport transforms iconic Star Citizen ships into finely crafted collectibles that bring the universe into your hands.

Built for the ‘verse, Monstertech’s Star Citizen flight chairs deliver unmatched comfort, precision, and immersion. Designed for pilots who demand realism and control, each chair is engineered with high-grade materials and modular components that adapt to every cockpit setup. Integrated mounts support joysticks, throttles, and peripherals from leading brands, allowing seamless transitions between combat, exploration, and trade. Every element, from ergonomic support to motion stability, is crafted to keep players fully engaged through long missions. Monstertech brings professional-grade simulation into the Star Citizen experience, transforming every flight into a truly tactile, pilot-ready adventure.

The Tobii Eye Tracker 5 brings Star Citizen to life by combining precise eye and head tracking for a fully immersive cockpit experience. Lean, glance, and track naturally to explore your ship, monitor displays, and maintain situational awareness in combat. Gaze selection lets you target enemies instantly, while Camera Boost enhances your movements for fluid control during dogfights and landings. Deep integration with Star Citizen enables full customization of sensitivity, tracking, and auto-centering. Tobii Eye Tracker 5 transforms flying from simply controlling a ship to becoming one with the cockpit, giving pilots a responsive, personal, and intuitive connection to the 'verse.

HCS VoicePacks brings immersive AI copilots to Star Citizen, enabling hands-free ship control and system management through natural voice interaction. Powered by VoiceAttack, their feature-rich Event Horizon profile evolves with every game update, keeping your AI copilot mission-ready. Legendary voices including William Shatner, Brent Spiner, Marina Sirtis, and Brian Blessed bring each character to life, giving your cockpit a unique personality and charm. As the leading provider of Star Citizen voice integration, HCS VoicePacks offers the most extensive library of interactive copilots, letting players fully experience the universe through intuitive, responsive voice control.

JRDF Printing LLC transforms digital Star Citizen ships into high-quality, 3D-printed model kits. Each collectible kit captures the intricate details of the original design, allowing fans to assemble, customize, and display authentic spacecraft. Advanced printing and artisan finishing ensure display-grade accuracy, while builders can personalize models with painting, weathering, and lighting. JRDF’s work bridges digital entertainment and physical creation, giving players a hands-on way to engage with the universe. From CitizenCon showcases to at-home assembly, JRDF inspires creativity, skill, and imagination, turning virtual ships into tangible pieces that celebrate both artistry and engineering.

FAQ FAQ What does it mean when a product is “officially licensed”? An officially licensed product is approved by us and developed in collaboration with our team. Each partner works under a license agreement that ensures accuracy, quality, and respect for the Star Citizen universe and its designs.

How can I tell if a product is genuine? Official items will clearly identify the licensee and may include our logo or an ‘Officially Licensed Product’ mark. If in doubt, check this page - if a company isn’t listed here, their products may not be officially licensed.

Where can I buy licensed products? Licensed products are sold directly through each partner’s own store or official retail channels. Links to partner websites are provided on this page.

Who handles customer service or shipping for these products? Each partner manages their own sales, shipping, and support. Please contact the relevant licensee directly with any product-specific questions.

Are there regional or shipping restrictions? Most licensees offer worldwide shipping, but availability and costs may vary by region. We recommend checking each partner’s store for details.

Will more partners be added in the future? Yes! We’re actively expanding our licensing program and will announce new partners as they join. Keep an eye on this page for updates.

We’ve got chills… they’re multiplying! Spooky season is creeping into the 'verse, and a month brimming with mischief awaits. From in-game challenges to fiendish contests that test your creativity to tricks and treats along the way, get ready for a frightfully fun time as we kick off our Day of the Vara festivities this October.

But before you dive headfirst into all the Spooktober shenanigans, a quick spell to keep things running smoothly: scheduled maintenance is lurking around the corner.

A maintenance window is planned for Tuesday, September 30th, 13:00–21:00 UTC for Platform and Web services.

We’re trying a new approach to reduce disruption - instead of full downtime, there will be brief partial outages for:

Login Services

Spectrum & Community Hub

Pledge Store

Most platform features will remain available during this window. This method lets us perform updates and validations while keeping disruption to a minimum. Thanks for your patience while we work to keep everything running wickedly well.

On Wednesday, we're welcoming the month of October by kicking off the Day of the Vara festivities!

body_html:
09/22/2025 - 7:30 PM This Week in Star Citizen Hello everyone, xē'suelen nyahyan

Last week packed a punch with an all new patch, a fresh Comms-Dive, and events both in-game and out!

Monday kicked off with the conclusion of the Race for Stanton event, with Hurston Dynamics claiming victory in the Regen Crisis! Citizens rallied to haul, mine, defend, and recover cargo to support the cause. By September 16, Hurston Dynamics had amassed a staggering 337,131,104 SCU, followed by microTech, Crusader, and then ArcCorp. Your efforts made this one for the UEE history books, and rewards have already been distributed, with more coming!

Comms-Dive #3 dropped Tuesday, answering a variety of your recent questions, covering everything from ship lights to incoming UI improvements. If you haven't yet, dive in on Spectrum!

A new episode of Behind the Ships introduced the RSI Apollo, the perfect remedy for injuries and adventuring mishaps. You can also explore the official RSI Apollo page and its dedicated Q&A to learn more about RSI's latest.

The week continued with a new patch release, Alpha 4.3.1: Virtue's Descent. We've been excited to see you all exploring the dangerous depths of the Onyx facilities. If you haven't accepted Arken Mallor's new mission yet, do so now and discover Project Hyperion and its new challenges, improved puzzles, balancing, and of course, loot!

Finally, over the weekend, the Bar Citizen World Tour landed in Rome, Italy. The team had an incredible time connecting in-person with the Italian community. Truly a special event! Big shoutout to all the organizers for putting together such a fantastic Bar Citizen!

These rules (“Rules”) apply to the 2955 | Horror Story Contest (“Contest”) carried out by Roberts Space Industries LLC and/or Roberts Space Industries International Limited (individually and collectively “RSI”) and their affiliates. Please read these Rules carefully. By submitting a Contest entry, you accept and agree to these Rules. If you do not agree to these Rules, any Contest entry submitted by you will be invalid and you will not be eligible to participate in the Contest or win a prize.

Eligibility – To participate in the Contest you must be at least eighteen (18) years of age and reside in a jurisdiction where the Contest and your participation is legally permitted. You must have an account with RSI and have agreed to the RSI Terms of Service (see: https://robertsspaceindustries.com/tos – the “RSI Terms”).
