title: Foundation Festival 2025 Org Spotlight
summary: During the lead-up to Foundation Festival 2025, we put out a call for organizations to show us what their community spirit was all about, and your response was incredible! We were blown away by the numerous outstanding submissions we received, and we appreciate everyone taking this opportunity to promote their organization.
body_html:
During the lead-up to Foundation Festival 2025, we put out a call for organizations to show us what their community spirit was all about, and your response was incredible! We were blown away by the numerous outstanding submissions we received, and we appreciate everyone taking this opportunity to promote their organization.

We wanted to shine the spotlight on some of your submissions from among the many worthy contenders. We hope you'll enjoy discovering the orgs in the gallery below, and you just might discover a new group of friends!

Ley Line Exotics Quick Info

Ley Line Exotics has been running dangerous trade missions in Star Citizen since its conception. They specialize in finding and trading the galaxy's most valuable exotic materials and items. They're treasure hunters and frontier traders who go where the money is good and the danger is real. If you want to make serious credits and have some excitement doing it, this is your crew.

Why should a new player join this org?

Don't know how to mine or trade? No problem. Their veteran members will teach you everything - from flying ships, to conquering contested zones, and finding the best trade routes. You'll have backup in dangerous areas, access to group resources, and learn the most profitable activities right away.

Link

Find the org page here.

The Unnamed Quick Info

The Unnamed is an 18+ community that welcomes players of all skill levels. They are a family that was founded on friendship, respect, and inclusivity. Whether you’re a miner, cargo hauler, mercenary, bounty hunter, medic, or explorer, The Unnamed has a place for you.

Why should a new player join this org?

The Unnamed is a community built on positivity, cooperation, and mutual respect. They host weekly events and collaborate with other friendly organizations in a relaxed, stress free setting. Finally, for those seeking personalized guidance, their community offers dedicated training through their Sherpa program. Sherpas provide one-on-one training with anyone, helping you navigate the game, get settled in the verse, and offer tailored support to ensure your success.

Link

Find the org page here.

Starkeeper Industries Quick Info

A relaxed, US-based Star Citizen org focused on cargo, combat, mining, and having a ridiculous amount of fun while doing it. They're a chaotic but tight-knit crew with weekly events, zero pressure, and just enough structure to keep things moving. Come for the stars, stay for the sarcasm! If you’re looking for a crew that’s more about fun and friendship than ranks and requirements, Starkeeper Industries is the perfect place to start your journey.

Why should a new player join this org?

We’ve all been there — staring at a terminal wondering how to pick up a box, trying to land without flipping over, or asking “wait, I have to refuel this thing??” Starkeeper Industries gets it, and they're the perfect group for new players who aren't sure where they should start out.

Link

Find the org page here.

Southern Cross Alliance Quick Info

Established in 2013, SCA is the largest social org for players from Australia and New Zealand. In addition to hosting Australia Bar Citizens, they founded the Crux Cup community eSports races with ANZIA Racing. SCA's specialization is industrialization and competition racing. They also focus on resource extraction, refinement, base building and crafting.

Why should a new player join this org?

As a comfortable place to play and start making friends, particularly in the Southern Hemisphere, you can join org events every Friday evening, jump into the next Bar Citizen for a drink, or take part in some of the greatest history-making eSports competitions in the 'verse.

Link

Find the org page here.

Northfield Quick Info

Northfield is a multifaceted legal organization made up of 3 main divisions: Security, Medical and Industrial. Additionally, they have smaller teams that pursue more specific gameplay elements such as racing (including hosting their own org races) and exploration.

Why should a new player join this org?

Welcoming to new players, Northfield features many veterans who love to share their experience and train new players. They enjoy teaching and passing on their knowledge to those who are new in the 'verse.

Link

Find the org page here.

All Trade Corporation Quick Info

All Trade Corporation is growing, with a shared passion for the game and all game loops offered as their members have combined various experiences. The organization takes a laid back approach as things in real life take priority, and they allow for time away from the game when needed.

Why should a new player join this org?

With members varying in age from 18 to the early 60's, All Trade Corporation welcomes players of all backgrounds, who enjoy sharing their unique experiences and knowledge with each other. This is the perfect place for new players who want to try a variety of game loops and learn what fits them best, all in a casual, supportive environment.

Link

Find the org page here.

NOVA Intergalactic Quick Info

While NOVA welcomes players from all locations, they prioritize effective communication through English as a common language and are focused on lawful gameplay professions.

Why should a new player join this org?

They take great pride in helping new players take their first steps into the verse. There is always someone available to chat with and answer your questions. NOVA even holds its own Beginners Guide class that help any new player get a firm grasp of the game and their community Discord.

Link

Find the org page here.

RPNet Quick Info

RPNet is the premiere method for connecting roleplayers and other organizations that focus purely on the roleplay aspect of Star Citizen. While also being a helpful community of roleplay fans, they do their best to tailor the experience to the player by assisting with missions, contracts, or other activities that may be difficult for solo players to complete.

Why should a new player join this org?

Roleplay is collaborative in nature, and those interested in pursuing deeper roleplay experiences will find a community who can help them further their craft. RPNet is also a safe, pro-LGBTQ+ space with a focus on ensuring their members feel at ease.

Link

Find the org page here.

United Colonial Force Quick Info

The United Colonial Force is a structured French-speaking organization focused on tactical security operations, infiltration, and space combat. They bring together dedicated players within an organized, demanding, and growth-oriented environment for those who want to sharpen their skills and play at a higher level. Their structure includes regular training sessions focused on advanced mechanics such as coordinated FPS combat, EVA maneuvers, boarding operations, multi-crew operations and dogfighting.

Why should a new player join this org?

Players looking to be part of a dedicated, welcoming team where new members are trained and supported will find a home here. Their members enjoy a stable, mature, and ambitious environment with a focus on fun. Both new and experienced players seeking structure, challenge, and growth are encouraged to join.

Link

Find the org page here.

Extensive Enterprises Quick Info

Extensive Enterprises—better known as EXTENT—is a tight-knit Star Citizen organization with a passion for exploration, teamwork, and immersive gameplay. They specialize in multi-crew operations and participate in all available lawful gameplay loops. Welcoming English and German speakers, they value skill-building, fun, and community events, whether in-game or at real-world locations.

Why should a new player join this org?

EXTENT is built on the belief that everyone matters. New players won’t be thrown in the deep end, as members are ready to provide connections, prepared manuals, and hands-on training. Weekend events offer structured opportunities to learn and grow, while their active Discord ensures you’re never flying alone.

Link

Find the org page here.

Black Star Initiative Quick Info

The Black Star Initiative (BSI) is a premier Private Military Company operating across the verse & all timezones, specializing in security operations, tactical missions, logistics, and commerce. They're a structured, mission-focused organization with a strong in-game presence and a global, active community.

Why should a new player join this org?

New to the ’verse? BSI offers guided onboarding, clear goals, and a supportive team environment to help you find your footing fast. You’ll always have someone to fly with, train with, and learn from—no pressure, just purpose. Whether you want to run missions, explore, PvP or grow your skills, BSI gives you the structure and support to thrive.

Link

Find the org page here.

PhaseOne Industries Quick Info

PhaseOne Industries is an established organization focused on industry and security with a hint of role playing. They enjoy sharing the experience and fun of Star Citizen through teamwork, squad tactics, and exploration. Have you always wanted to crew or captain in a fleet operation? Join PhaseOne and live out that dream! While they are interested in all aspects of SC, they lean into Industry and trade alongside security operations. Core members have an extensive knowledge base in game mechanics and are always willing to assist new and existing players.

Why should a new player join this org?

They have friendly orgmates that are always willing to guide new players. Their members take part in Combined Arms and Fleet Battle events that showcase the true potential of Star Citizen. PhaseOne caters to all aspects of Star Citizen except for piracy.

Link

Find the org page here.

INVFED Quick Info

INVFED is a fleet-based organization built around two core divisions: one focused on space, and FPS combat, while the other is dedicated to industry gameplay. They host regular events across both divisions, and as the game grows, they're preparing for future systems like base-building and deeper economic play. Whether you're in it for the action or the profits, INVFED offers a structured, community-driven environment that makes your time in the ‘verse more rewarding.

Why should a new player join this org?

Whether you’re new or experienced, INVFED offers clear organization, regular events, and a friendly, supportive community. They value flexible playstyles and schedules, giving members room to grow, learn, and take on leadership roles if they choose. This is an org built for structure, teamwork, progression, and having fun in the ‘verse.

Link

Find the org page here.

Even Legion Quick Info

Even Legion is a highly active and organized Star Citizen group built around server events, strong camaraderie, and a commitment to long-term community growth. Created by Star Citizen YouTuber EvenLease, they maintain dedicated divisions for combat, industrial, and medical operations - with room for every playstyle, from casual to elite.

Why should a new player join this org?

With roughly 12 events per week, there’s always something happening in the Legion! From large ops to small group missions, new players never have to wonder what to do or where to start. There’s always a clear place to hop right in. They also have a dedicated role for new players and volunteer guides who are always around to help answer questions and provide support. No attendance or activity requirements! Whether you’re brand new or returning, this is a place where you belong.

Link

Find the org page here.

Quantum Jump Medical Quick Info

Operating for nearly 9 years, Quantum Jump Medical offers a huge range of services for: medical, security, transport, refueling, logistic operations, and much more. They provide all these services for free, even refunding the beacon fee to the client. They've established many partnerships, the largest being the medical provider for ATMO eSports. Quantum Jump Medical is always "Just A Jump Away"!

Why should a new player join this org?

They provide easy-to-follow tutorial videos like "how to spawn a ship," as well as Quantum Academy, which includes course-specific training with a QJM instructor who will provide knowledge on how to do virtually any type of gameplay the 'verse offers. This includes basic and advanced flight, FPS missions, cargo, salvage, mining, medical, and much more.

Link

Find the org page here.

Sol Armada Quick Info

With multiple weekly events, over 50 active players, and a decade of experience, Sol Armada consistently provides members with a friendly, reliable group to enjoy Star Citizen's content with. Event designs and clear briefings grant members a clearly structured gameplay experience. Sol Armada: Your fleet, your fun, delivered!

Why should a new player join this org?

Sol Armada has several player Guides, and their combined members have successfully completed hundreds of sessions in the Guide System. If you want to learn something, they can easily link you up with an experienced player to guide you. They'll show you how to get started on flying and earning credits, so you'll be able to earn the ship(s) of your dreams in no time.

Link

Find the org page here.

S.T.A.R.D.U.S.T. Quick Info

S.T.A.R.D.U.S.T. isn't your average org. They're PvPvE -focused, drama-free, and built around a foundation of kindness, structure, and community. They offer active leadership, are LGBTQ+ inclusive, judgment-free, and real-life-first. A place to play, create, laugh, train, and grow. You’re not just joining an org—you’re joining your org. A place where your voice matters, your gameplay is valued, and your goals become our goals.

Why should a new player join this org?

They don’t just fly ships - they build things together. From event planning to lore-inspired missions, members regularly contribute to video production, game testing, tool creation, and community events. If you have a project idea, odds are someone else here wants to help bring it to life. For those just starting out, they pair experienced players with newer pilots for 1-on-1 guidance - not just ship certs and gear handouts, but practical training on contracts, navigation, and survivability. They don’t leave anyone lost in space. Whether you’re a quiet hauler, a support main, a fleet ops lead, or a meme-generating bard, you’re welcome here. Their crew spans time zones, playstyles, and skill levels - and they like it that way.

Link

Find the org page here.

RIP Squad Quick Info

RIP Squad (RS) is a welcoming organization with vast knowledge of the ‘verse and the skills required to navigate it. With its roots in salvaging and industrial professions, RS has grown their roster with like-minded members who enjoy various types of gameplay, from mining to high-risk operations such as Hathor, Storm Breaker, bounty hunting, and more. They continue to cultivate a warm and friendly environment that citizens love to be a part of, and you can be too!

Why should a new player join this org?

Many of RIP Squad's members are registered as guides and focus on other citizens in the 'verse who may need assistance. Their leadership has composed a series of course modules for new citizens, which they call their Foundations course - a nod to the Foundation Festival. This course is designed to teach new citizens how to navigate cities and ships, manage inventory, fly, defend themselves, and fight both in the air and on the ground. Many who have completed this course have since become instructors and guides themselves. They take pride in the rapid progress of new members and are committed to providing a strong foundation while giving you a home among the stars!

Link

Find the org page here.

Linux Users Group Quick Info

Operating since 2014, Linux Users Group (LUG) came into existence through a shared love for both Star Citizen and Linux systems. Their community is made up of veterans who've mastered the art of Linux gaming, as well as curious newcomers just discovering the operating system. No matter where you are on your Linux journey, you'll feel right at home here. They believe in growing together, learning from one another, and celebrating their shared passion for open-source power in gaming!

Why should a new player join this org?

They're a diverse and welcoming community of Linux users who love helping each other out. LUG offers community support, wiki resources, a quick start guide with troubleshooting tips, weekly gatherings, and other helpful resources. Their custom tool takes the hassle out of installing and managing Star Citizen on your Linux system so you can focus on exploring the 'verse!

Link

Find the org page here.

Shadow Guardians Quick Info

Shadow Guardians is a Brazilian Star Citizen organization dedicated to becoming a leading force in the verse's endgame content. They support both veterans and new players through a well-structured ecosystem of training, services, and community events. Driven by camaraderie, integrity, and organization, their mission is to empower members to take center stage in the universe of Star Citizen by fostering growth, teamwork, and memorable experiences.

Why should a new player join this org?

Shadow Guardians was carefully built to be the perfect starting point for new players entering the Star Citizen universe. They offer dedicated flight instructors and a full training program for beginners, from basic controls to advanced dogfighting. In areas like hauling, mining, and salvage, experienced members regularly share practical tips and techniques to help newcomers grow with confidence. Shadow Guardians provides a place where new players can make friends, learn the ropes, and enjoy meaningful group experiences right from the start.

Link

Find the org page here.

Starhead Federation Quick Info

The Starhead Federation was founded to create a community grounded in the values of diversity, cooperation, and fairness. They believe every individual has the potential to achieve great things and that the community becomes stronger as more people join. They are committed to building an environment where everyone feels welcome and safe. Believing in the power of friendship and collaboration, they aim to grow a strong and resilient community. The community consists of adventurers, traders, miners, racers, fighters, and players of all kinds. They provide a wide range of activities and opportunities, allowing each member to grow and refine their skills. They are determined to face the challenges presented by the 'verse and to continue evolving. They believe that each individual has the potential to achieve great things and that together they are invincible. The org regularly holds events and provides all kinds of help, whether on Spectrum or Discord. But in all their endeavors and adventures, one thing always comes first: fun and fairness. They are a community that strives to create an environment where everyone is treated with respect and has the chance to do their best. And at the end of the day, the most important message should be: “It's just a game.”

Why should a new player join this org?

As one of the largest German-speaking organization, Starhead Federation covers all aspects of the game and invites everyone, regardless of whether they are casual or pro, to join. They offer new players many opportunities to take their first steps in the game. With their versatile squads, you have the opportunity to experience and learn about industry, combat, exploration or fun. Regular organizational events give new members the opportunity to quickly integrate into groups and find the path that suits them best.

Link

Find the org page here.

Medrunner Services Quick Info

Medrunner is focused on one clear goal; to provide premium emergency medical response and extraction services. They independently train and field highly effective medical response teams composed of Medical Technicians, Security Specialists, and Pilots that can go up against the worst odds and come out with a healthy client. When not out saving other Citizens, members of Medrunner can be found running contracts together, working on video projects, setting up group training and testing exercises, or just chatting and hanging out. With one common goal but many varied interests, there is always something new and fun to learn in Medrunner.

Why should a new player join this org?

Medrunners offers a high standard of training, and even players who have very little experience can participate in their activities without feeling unprepared or uncomfortable. One Medrunner, who joined the Organization in June 2025 had this to say on the subject: “Since a year ago, I vowed that eventually I would start playing Star Citizen, by joining this organization. I just believed that I wasn't ready, I didn't have the HOSAS setup I wanted, nor did I feel confident in joining any community since I usually play solo. I wanted to see what a community like it had to offer beyond its services to the rest of the 'Verse's audience, because as a solo player that struggles to befriend others, I didn't believe that a community could be accommodating to me. Medrunner has such a vast community that is willing to teach you the basics of Star Citizen, I found myself seamlessly adapting to the nature of its current state without much complaint.”

Link

Find the org page here.

THE CUBE Quick Info

THE CUBE is made up of players who want to support each other in their time in the 'verse, as well as test new features and push the game to its limits! They have four divisions of focus: Fleet (air support), Infantry (ground vehicle and FPS combat), Industry (mining, salvaging and hauling), and Support (medical, rescue and logistics) where they provide training and certifications to members for these activities. Their leaders provide bi-weekly events that utilize these divisions, such as participating in the "Storm Breaker" sandbox activity, where all four divisional teams have a specific role to play. They also have occasional events designed to drop jaws in awe—such as massive, coordinated fleet battles, skies filled with thousands of missiles, or an entire conga line of heavy armor units. Other weekly events include Arena Commander basic training sessions for newer pilots, Industry Monday events for stockpiling resources and Infantry Training for better ground coordination. THE CUBE welcomes active players who wish to have this be their primary org. While the organization maintains a family-friendly environment, there is an age requirement of 18+ to join.

Why should a new player join this org?

THE CUBE has lots of friendly, familiar faces who are active during most times of day, so it will always feel safe for someone to jump into any channel and immediately start playing. Their active and welcoming player base is always more than happy to give you a helping hand in your journey. THE CUBE consists of players of a very diverse age range and skill level, so it's very easy to fit in with people who fit your style of play.

Link

Find the org page here.

The United Star Force Quick Info

The United Star Force is a self-sustained PMC that surveys the vast expanse of space, pushing the boundaries of science. Capable of committing to every aspect of gameplay Star Citizen has to offer, their primary missions are to explore the galaxy to gather resources and to fulfill manufacturing operations, and to provide search and rescue services. With these objectives in mind, they prioritize aid to citizens who find themselves stranded too far from civilization. USF is dedicated to combating the pirates and criminal syndicates who obstruct the well-being of innocent citizens and are a hindrance to the sustainability and progression of the Empire. They are a brotherhood of like-minded individuals dedicated to a single cause: justice.

Why should a new player join this org?

The org helps new players learn the basics and fundamentals of Star Citizen, and helps veterans of the game get up to speed with how the organization operates. During their time as a recruit, new members learn how to navigate different gameplay mechanics, the structure of the USF, their community guidelines, and much more. New players learn how to fly their ship, be efficient in all forms of combat, and how to be a valuable member of a team. Once a member graduates the USF Academy they gain access to private operations. They hold weekly events in the form of Field Training Exercises specifically designed to teach and certify members how to fulfill their chosen occupations. The goal is to give their members the ability to specialize in any occupational field they choose and teach them how to become experts in the interests they have. When a member is certified, requisition programs give them the ability to request funds from the organization bank to help them purchase ships, components, and ship weapons.

Link

Find the org page here.

Knights Of Sidonia Quick Info

Knights of Sidonia (KOS) is a lawful organization in Star Citizen, specializing in UEE paramilitary operations, transport, exploration, and many other lawful gameplay loops. They welcome both new and veteran players across all professions—whether someone is a combat pilot, trader, miner, medic, or infantry specialist. Operating primarily in North American time zones, KOS hosts official Org Nights every Friday (7:30 PM CST) and Saturday (8:00 PM CST), with members active throughout the week. Their growing fleet emphasizes structured roles and functional teamwork over strict roleplay. Their ethos and ethics ensure a fun, organized, and welcoming environment for all.

Why should a new player join this org?

The KOS is built with both new and veteran players in mind. As a lawful organization, they offer a wide range of activities, giving new players the freedom to discover what they enjoy most in Star Citizen. What truly sets KOS apart for recruits is their commitment to structured learning and mentorship. They offer customized training courses designed to help players develop the skills necessary to navigate the game with confidence and effectiveness. Whether you're flying your first ship or setting foot on a hostile moon, you're never alone - they're here to help you grow.

Link

Find the org page here.

Elite BR Quick Info

Elite BR is a vibrant and welcoming Brazilian community in Star Citizen, bringing together players of all playstyles — from traders and explorers to security and logistics crews. Their mission is to create a supportive and fun environment where members can grow together, share experiences, and build lasting friendships in the verse.

Why should a new player join this org?

They believe no one should explore the ‘verse alone. They’ve built a strong support structure for new players, including: a highly active Discord server with experienced members ready to assist, frequent events focused on learning and cooperation, mentorship through hands-on activities like mining, cargo hauling, and combat training, and a culture that values kindness, inclusion, and teamwork above all. They also encourage responsible use of the Guide System and Referral Program, helping newcomers find their place in the universe with confidence. Whether you're just starting your journey or returning after time away, Elite BR is a home for all — focused on collaboration, shared knowledge, and community-driven gameplay.

Link

Find the org page here.

Garden Interstellar Initiative Quick Info

The Garden Interstellar Initiative GII is an org by Space Tomato Gaming focused on creating the best gameplay opportunities for solo and group-focused players interested in any kind of gameplay. They have 2 main rules: No non-consensual PVP, and real life comes first. They typically abide by the general law of the area, but conduct business as needed in the org's interests. For those interested in exploration, crafting, security, or mining—and looking to experience real progression while doing so and much more, GII is worth checking out.

Why should a new player join this org?

Star Citizen can be a lot when starting out. But there are many possibilities. Group mining adventures, massive 50+ person fleet battles, small FPS squads, group bounty hunting, or simply learning how to fly your ship. GII can help you meet your goals in-game through regular events, new player help channels, an org-exclusive Star Citizen progression system, and any support you need for your solo gameplay. Whether you're science, industrial, or security-focused, they can help you get the most out of the verse. The Garden Grows!

Link

Find the org page here.

Pico's Task Force Quick Info

Pico’s Task Force (PTF) is a casual private military org that started as a meme by strapping the in-game Pico plushie into every ship they flew. That joke turned into something real: a tight-knit crew focused on security, medical support, mentorship, and storytelling. They mix light roleplay and custom lore with late-night ops, real camaraderie, and a zero-pressure vibe. Whether someone is a fresh face or a grizzled vet, PTF offers purpose-driven gameplay and a community that actually feels like a crew. They’re not here to flex, they’re here to show up.

Why should a new player join this org?

Star Citizen can be a bit overwhelming at first, which is exactly why PTF was formed. They actively seek out new players, not just to pad numbers, but to guide them and give them a crew they can lean on. They teach mechanics, provide backup, and make sure you’re not going through the chaos alone. You’ll get real support from players who want to help, not lecture. In PTF, new players aren’t background noise, they’re the mission. From your first bunker run to your first med evac, you’ll have people watching your six and helping you figure things out. They've all been there, and they make sure you don’t go through it solo.

Link

Find the org page here.

Sibylla Quick Info

Sibylla is a multi-role organization with the goal of taking part in Star Citizen’s largest events, both PVP and PVE. They were originally created as an immediate and rapid response to the Vanduul raids that were devastating the UEE. Protecting humanity from these threats remains their core purpose. They have become fully autonomous since then, in terms of operations and internal management. This evolution is a response to the needs of the 'verse and its citizens, now and in the future.

Why should a new player join this org?

Sibylla is a welcoming organization for both new players and veterans alike. They have an advanced onboarding system to guide new members, including a mentorship program. A wide range of training modules is available to support players of any skill level. All of this is aimed at delivering high-quality, advanced events for their community, which you can be a part of!

Link

Find the org page here.

Vanguard Defense Solutions Quick Info

Vanguard Defense Solutions is a lawful private military company dedicated to safeguarding the 'verse through professionalism, unity, and ethical service. Founded by former UEE veterans and elite mercenaries, VDS brings together operatives from all walks of life to provide secure, reliable solutions in even the most hostile corners of space. From counter-piracy operations in Stanton to humanitarian escort missions in Pyro space, they stand on the front lines to protect those who cannot protect themselves.

Why should a new player join this org?

Whether you're brand new to Star Citizen or a returning player after a break, VDS attempts to teach and bring everyone who joins the organization up to speed in their chosen niche (mercenary missions, PVP, and other aspects of the game). Although they are a mercenary organization, they also accommodate players who enjoy mining, salvaging, hauling, and other industrial roles. VDS is also very active with members who participate nightly in several parts of the game.

Link

Find the org page here.

Los Incorregibles Intergalactic Cartel Quick Info

This casual roleplaying organization, affiliated with The Syndicate, was founded by a group of UEE veterans who felt betrayed by the UEE following the events of Vega 2. They have since opted to grow in numbers, operating by their own rules while dedicating themselves to piracy, smuggling and other criminal activities, but also helping on lawful operations if they find it beneficial.

Why should a new player join this org?

This predominantly Spanish-speaking org helps many new players whether they become members or not, assisting others with the basics of the game such as equipment, flight lessons, FPS lessons, ship mechanics and game rules. The org also has many ships available to test and fly, so they do not require new members to have anything beyond a basic game package. With members who are committed to the project, they love training new players!

Link

Find the org page here.

Black Sheep Quick Info

Founded in 2017, this organization’s primary goal is to have fun without overthinking. With around 100 members, they regularly organize small events such as the Cyclone Trophy, a race they've been hosting for four years. They are pro-UEE and have future plans to establish a land base to fight alongside UEE forces. Lawful players looking for adventure are encouraged to apply.

Why should a new player join this org?

Black Sheep regularly has new players joining their ranks. They love to have fun, laugh, and enjoy the game, always in a good mood. Most of their members are players who recently joined Star Citizen and who stayed around to continue to discover all that the game had to offer. The organization always enjoys introducing new players to Star Citizen, so give them a try!

Link

Find the org page here.

Redscar Nomads Quick Info

Upon meeting vagrants like themselves, The Founders lit the first bonfire, a wayfaring beacon in the void. Vagrants alike found refuge there, and formed the first flotilla of Redscar Nomads. Since then, Nomads survive and wander, committing themselves to making contributions to the Eternal Voyage.

Why should a new player join this org?

All are welcome around the bonfire. Whether you’re looking to pew pew, go fast, or kick back with some tunes, citizens can find camaraderie and support on the Redscar flotilla. Veteran Nomads will assist vagrant rookies as they learn to fly, fetch, and flourish in the ‘verse.

Link

Find the org page here.

Légion Écarlate Quick Info

A predominantly French-speaking org, their goal is, and will always be, the exploration of mysterious and sometimes dangerous places, without seeking profitability. Their funding comes from other activities focused on combat and industry, allowing them to fully dedicate ourselves to this passion they hold dear, without worrying about income from it.

Why should a new player join this org?

They're a small and relaxed group who are always happy to help out new players. Since they're not a huge org, it’s easy to find your place and not feel overwhelmed. Everyone knows each other, and there’s no pressure, just good vibes, fun exploration, and a crew that’s got your back while you learn the ropes.

Link

Find the org page here.

Stellar Eagle Alliance Quick Info

Stellar Eagle Alliance (SEA) is the largest Star Citizen organization in Denmark and a proud part of the wider Nordic community. They’re best known for The Experience – the first cinematic in-game cruise of its kind in the ‘verse – and for hosting a wide range of immersive exploration, adventure, and PvP events that bring players together across borders.

Why should a new player join this org?

This Danish org is made up of explorers, miners, cargo haulers, adventurers, traders, PvPers, and storytellers. They create. They connect. They lead. Join them – and be part of something greater: a Star Citizen community and social network for Danes with over 330 members, reaching far beyond the boundaries of the known ‘verse.

Link

Find the org page here.

Synchronizerz Quick Info

Synchronizerz was founded in June 2016 as a global community from many countries and time zones. They aim to provide a friendly, fun, and supportive atmosphere, enabling members and allies to accomplish greater success in unity than they can apart. Their motto: together, we rise!

Why should a new player join this org?

Synchronizerz is a perfect fit for any player who leads with and lives by the values of teamwork, excellence, integrity, and respect. Every citizen, new and veteran, is valued. Whether your goal is to become an expert navigator, ace pilot, rugged explorer, feisty combat specialist, or industry magnate, you can meet other like-minded players who are willing to assist you. Never go into the cold darkness of the ‘verse alone and unprotected. This is your home base. Join them!

Link

Find the org page here.

Galactic Police Department Quick Info

The Galactic Police Department (GPD) is a service-oriented organization focused on law enforcement, public safety, and community support across the ‘Verse. Their interests include protecting citizens in need, maintaining order, mentoring new players, and engaging in immersive patrols and operations. From foot patrols in city streets to full-scale investigations in deep space, GPD is committed to creating a fun, structured, and impactful presence wherever they operate.

Why should a new player join this org?

GPD is an ideal organization for new players because they prioritize mentorship, guidance, and teamwork. Their officers regularly assist new citizens by offering hands-on support, training, and ride-alongs through key locations. They'll help you learn the ropes, navigate the game’s systems, and feel part of a close-knit, active community. Whether you’re looking to serve, learn, or just be part of something meaningful, the GPD will have your back from day one.

Link

Find the org page here.

Event Concept Association Quick Info

Event Concept Association is the galaxy's leading specialized event agency. They have already organized several gigantic spaceship exhibitions, air shows, and aerial acrobatics festivals, as well as open days for several corporations in unique and prestigious locations. Several dozen corporations have already been won over by their events, and they continue to attract an ever-growing audience!

Why should a new player join this org?

The Event Concept Association isn't a corporation or union; it's more of an association; a volunteer organization from across the galaxy dedicated to helping organize complex events for the general public. If you enjoy organizing popular events like air shows or large open houses on an outpost with a collection of starships to tour, this is the group for you! Their members come from dozens of different organizations to help out, and as such, often become ambassadors, inviting their friends to the events.

Link

Find the org page here.

Oracle Research Quick Info

Oracle Research is a sovereign science, exploration, and intelligence organization founded on the belief that the truth of the 'verse lies buried beneath its ruins, waiting to be decrypted. They operate at the nexus of historical recovery, experimental science, and strategic autonomy. Oracle Research is not a military faction, nor a corporate extension; it is an evolving archive. They are survivors turned explorers, tacticians, researchers, and mentors who now guide the next generation of citizens to continue the mission. Their activities range from artifact recovery and site investigation to tactical mentorship and reconnaissance logistics. They combine academic discipline with field-tested experience to guide their members and protect new citizens venturing into the unknown.

Why should a new player join this org?

Oracle Research exists to guide, not command. They understand the chaos and complexity new citizens face and respond not with demands, but with mentorship, clarity, and community. Players interested in science, exploration, history, and lore will find themselves right at home.

Link

Find the org page here.

EXPANSE UNION Quick Info

EXPANSE UNION is a disciplined and ideologically-driven Star Citizen organization. They focus on structured gameplay, tactical cooperation, and onboarding through their unique Sputnik web platform. Guided by the Codex, they offer recruits clear roles in the Civilian Corps, Army, or Academy — with contracts, mentorship, and purpose at every step.

Why should a new player join this org?

At EXPANSE UNION, they believe that meeting every new recruit is the beginning of a story worth being proud of. Even the very first interview is not a formality, but a true starting point on the path within a team that values respectful communication. This simple tradition helps set the right tone and build trust from the very first moments. In addition to advice and support, they offer a full-fledged web platform, the academy: Sputnik. Here, their specialists create guides, gameplay knowledge tests, themed quests, and dynamic activities. By completing them, a recruit gains mastery of key mechanics and becomes a confident player - ready for everything and most importantly - ready to help others.

Link

Find the org page here.

Wayfarers Quick Info

This is a close-knit crew who explores all Star Citizen has to offer. Born under different stars, bonded by a shared restlessness, and drawn to the thrill of discovery, they are wanderers on a journey of adventure. Here, settlers, traders, and dreamers coexist for a purpose larger than themselves, a beacon that calls to them as they chart their course through the cosmos. They move to an offbeat rhythm with plenty of laughs, grudges, and unexpected moments in between. Regularly outgunned, and always outnumbered, they stand ready when the stakes are high, often finding themselves on the run. Bound by loyalty, their promise is simple: stand together, no matter the odds. Fearless, daring and free; they are at home among the stars.

Why should a new player join this org?

This is the perfect org for a new player to join because the Wayfarers always find an adventure! They may be small, but they always make the most of Star Citizen: whether they're hijacking an Idris, hauling high-value cargo, squeezing bombs through airlocks, rescuing someone from a bunker, or enjoying a country music night in a Reclaimer, no one is having more fun in the 'verse than them. They love welcoming new players into the crew because the only thing better than chasing adventure is sharing it with someone new. Just bring your helmet: they’ll handle the mischief.

Link

Find the org page here.

4th Fleet Auxiliary Quick Info

The 4th Fleet is a semi-roleplay, military simulation org comprised of a wide variety of individuals from around the world with a shared interest in Star Citizen, community and cooperation. They've based their lore heavily within the SC universe and try to operate within the bounds of the UEE Navy including lawful gameplay such as security and law enforcement, haulage and emergency service. They've already held a few very successful in-org events including operations Stone Bounty and Serpent Flame. If you've ever wanted to belong to a group where you're more than just a number on a page, 4th Fleet can be that experience. You'll be joining a small group of friends for whom a love for Star Citizen is the core of the experience. Goals and ambition are the benefit, not the rule, and this group is always eager to have you join as a new friend.

Why should a new player join this org?

The 4th Fleet is open to not only teaching new members how they do things, but also learning from their members new and old to better improve the quality of play for everyone. They have a comprehensive system for internal ranking and merits to be earned for people who show exceptionalism. With players from all across Star Citizen's various gameplay loops, they've got something for everyone, from simple medical gameplay all the way up to entire fleet coordination. They're also fairly relaxed as an org, and respect that their members' real lives come first, operating around such obligations instead of "cherry picking" members to suit a hardline policy set.

Link

Find the org page here.

PentaCore Dynamics Quick Info

PentaCore Dynamics is a German-speaking organization where every play style is welcome, whether mining or salvage, in Stanton or Pyro, with capital ship or small fighter, whether PVE or PVP. They do not dictate how anyone plays the game, up to the point where another player’s experience is negatively affected by unfair means. They plan to specialize in base building and crafting in the future, and are willing to assist other organizations within these areas. They are always open to forming new, meaningful alliances with other orgs, regardless of whether they are military or purely economic. They are also happy to offer military support for current and future sandbox activities in the 'verse.

Why should a new player join this org?

As a a very active org with regular group events, they love taking along new players and introducing them to Star Citizen's gameplay. They are a mixed group, with members ranging from their early 20s to their mid-50s, and all ages are welcome here. Home to players of all skill levels, they follow the motto that every citizen was once just starting their journey. Experienced players are always on hand with help and advice and are happy to answer any questions that arise. PentaCore Dynamics represents every style of play, so everyone will feel they belong. They're a colorful group that has fun with the vision of Star Citizen and would like to share this fun with you.

Link

Find the org page here.

Krampus Quick Info

Krampus is an Italian industrial organization aiming to evolve into the Unite Resource Worker guild. Rather than a military group, they are ordinary workers, engineers, and miners who, aware of the dangers of space, are ready to defend themselves from any and all threats. Their motto is: wreckers by profession, miners by passion, and fighters by necessity. Krampus welcomes both new and veteran players without forcing them to join the org right away: players simply hop into Discord and play. If, after a few months, someone feels at home, they can discuss joining the org while sitting in the Reclaimer mess hall over a fresh Cruz.

Why should a new player join this org?

Following several of their members' experiences with previous orgs, they realized that the hierarchies and constraints of many organizations made it complicated for new players to join a new group and ask for help. Krampus has members who spend evenings instructing new players, and will frequently offer to accompany those who would like to test new ships. They'll also acquaint new members with every aspect of the game as much as possible, and direct them on which package to choose if they want to stay. They're willing to help those who may only have a starter ship to acquire new ships quickly, either by doing missions or in contests. They want those who play with them to feel like they are part of a family, and will help to make your time in the 'verse as relaxed as possible.

Link

Find the org page here.

Didn't find what you're looking for? Check out our Organizations system—Star Citizen has a wealth of orgs just waiting to be discovered.

title: Q&A: Esperia Prowler Utility
summary: Q&A Prowler Utility by Esperia Welcome the Prowler Utility, a new recreation for seamless hauling available to fly with the Alpha 4.2 patch release. Like its predecessor, this new variant honors the organic design of the infamous Tevarin ship entrusted to Esperia years ago, with additional storage and comprehensive weaponry.
body_html:
Q&A Prowler Utility by Esperia Welcome the Prowler Utility, a new recreation for seamless hauling available to fly with the Alpha 4.2 patch release. Like its predecessor, this new variant honors the organic design of the infamous Tevarin ship entrusted to Esperia years ago, with additional storage and comprehensive weaponry.

We asked the Vehicle and Gameplay teams a few questions about the Prowler Utility. Here are the answers, straight from the devs themselves.

One of the Esperia Prowler’s key strengths is its stealth. Can we expect similar low-signature performance from the Utility variant? Currently, the base Prowler is slightly stealthier than the Utility due to its military application. The Utility’s larger physical footprint and additional external features, like winglets and cargo doors, result in a slightly higher signature. That said, while the original dropship variant of the Esperia Prowler remains a top performer in terms of stealth, the Utility variant still boasts a strong stealth profile. It may be slightly less effective, but it remains more than capable of discreetly moving valuable cargo across the 'verse.

With 32 SCU of cargo capacity, what container configurations can I use on each side of the ship? For example, would ‘32 x 1 SCU’ or ‘2 x 16 SCU’ boxes work? Yes, both cargo grids are designed to support all sized containers up to 16 SCU, so both examples are valid.

Does the Utility variant have the same limited quantum fuel capacity as the original dropship version? Is it mainly intended for short-range transport? The Utility variant currently features a slightly larger quantum fuel tank (2.25 SCU compared to the base variant’s 2 SCU) as well as a modest increase in hydrogen capacity. While still best suited for shorter-range missions, these upgrades provide a bit more operational flexibility for transport-focused tasks.

What distinguishes the Prowler Utility from other cargo haulers? It’s a rare blend of stealth and capability. With its aggressive aesthetic, solid defenses, and ability to operate under the radar, the Prowler Utility stands out as an excellent stealth-oriented alien cargo ship.

Does it offer any unique features? Its combination of stealth and cargo functionality makes it unique. It’s currently the only alien cargo ship designed with a stealth profile in mind.

Are you doing anything to improve the original Prowler alongside this new variant? Yes, with Alpha 4.2.0, we're addressing a number of longstanding concerns with the base Prowler, some of which carry over to the new Utility and both Talon as well:

Critical HP values are being increased.

Armor Damage Protection is being increased.

SCM max speed is being increased.

Quantum Fuel Capacity is being slightly increased (This adjustment carries over to the Utility).

The damage effect on flight performance is being adjusted, with a reduction in the causes of less uncontrollable Torque Imbalance when thrusters are destroyed. (This fix carries over to the Utility and the Talon, as well).

Is it equipped with a tractor beam for cargo handling? Yes, it includes a deployable Size 2 remote tractor turret. Additionally, unlike the base model, its redesigned wing feathers now fold upward in landing mode, making cargo loading much easier.

The Utility variant includes a pilot seat, co-pilot seat, and three jump seats. How do you envision players using it? Can you give an example scenario? The jump seats allow for a small crew or a few passengers in a pinch. Primarily, this is a stealth-oriented medium freight ship with defensive capabilities far above average for its size, featuring 2x S3 and 2x S4 weapons and 4x S2 shield generators.

It’s ideal for high-risk zones like Jumptown, settlements in Pyro, or smuggling runs. The integrated tractor beam and large cargo doors let the co-pilot assist with cargo collection even mid-flight, enabling quick getaways without having to land.

DISCLAIMER These answers accurately reflect development's intentions at the time of writing, but the company and development team reserve the right to adapt, improve, or change feature and ship designs in response to feedback, playtesting, design revisions, or other considerations to improve balance or the quality of the game overall.

title: July 2025 Subscriber Promotions
summary: Alpha 4.2: Storm Breaker is LIVE in the Persistent Universe!
body_html:
Alpha 4.2: Storm Breaker is LIVE in the Persistent Universe!

Whether you’re heading out to uncover the secrets of the storm, exploring locked-down research facilities, or simply keeping the wheels of commerce turning, July’s Vehicle of the Month has your back. Built for long-distance hauling in the most dangerous systems, the MISC Starlancer MAX is the perfect ally on any mission. This month’s Flair features cargo-themed collectibles that will add a cute yet industrial touch to your hangar.

IN-GAME REWARDS (FLAIR) July’s Flair is all about compact cargo, with collections of cuddly and decorative SCU containers that will brighten up any hangar or ship’s hab.

Earnable In-Game: Our goal is to make most items earnable in-game. For this reason, many flair items have been added to the in-game loot table as rare drops from Alpha 3.17. Most pre-2023 items that can be carried by players are available now, with new and future flair being added after a three-month exclusivity window.

Some exclusive digital event items, such as those from CitizenCon Goodies Packs, will not be discoverable via the in-game loot system.

This item will be delivered in an upcoming patch.

Current Imperator-level Subscribers get this item and the above Centurion-level item as part of their subscriptions.

This item will be delivered in an upcoming patch.

This item is available for all Subscribers to pledge for in the dedicated Subscriber Store.

These items will be delivered in an upcoming patch.

MISC Starlancer MAX and Drake Caterpillar Centurion Subscribers: MISC Starlancer MAX (with 12-month insurance) MISC Starlancer MAX: Built to haul heavy loads across the most treacherous star systems. The Starlancer MAX’s huge cargo hold and staunch defenses make it the ideal way to take on the newest challenges of the ‘verse.

Imperator Subscribers: Drake Caterpillar and MISC Starlancer MAX (with 24-month insurance) Drake Caterpillar: An icon of “privateer” hauling and bona fide classic. Heavily defended and built for danger, the Caterpillar utilizes Drake’s rough-and-ready approach to shipbuilding for heavyweight hauling.

MISC Starlancer MAX: Built to haul heavy loads across the most treacherous star systems. The Starlancer MAX’s huge cargo hold and staunch defenses make it the ideal way to take on the newest challenges of the ‘verse.

Store. Centurion Subscribers receive 10% off merchandise, while Imperator

Subscribers receive 15% off. Take advantage of this perk and peruse the

selection of available merchandise including jackets, hoodies, shirts, mugs,

hats, mousepads, stickers, and more.

Subscriber Store. You can fill in any gaps, pick up store-only items, or

grab extras to gift to non-Subscribers from the My Hangar section of your

RSI profile.

NOT A SUBSCRIBER?

If you would like to receive this flair as part of a subscription, you can subscribe before July 7, 2025 (20:00 UTC). Otherwise, you can pick up these and previous months’ flair (going back to 2014) in the dedicated Subscriber Store.

summary: Alien Week 2955 – Wikelo’s Nine Tastes Contest

Alien Week 2955 – Wikelo’s Nine Tastes Contest

title: Star Citizen Monthly Report: May 2025
summary: PU Monthly Report May 2025 Alpha 4.2: Storm Breaker is live in the Public Test Universe! There’s still a lot to do behind the scenes as the new content gets pushed to the breaking point in preparation for Live release. Alongside patch fixes and other various changes, many teams touched on tech, locations, and updates coming later this year. Read on for all the latest info.
body_html:
PU Monthly Report May 2025 Alpha 4.2: Storm Breaker is live in the Public Test Universe! There’s still a lot to do behind the scenes as the new content gets pushed to the breaking point in preparation for Live release. Alongside patch fixes and other various changes, many teams touched on tech, locations, and updates coming later this year. Read on for all the latest info.

AI Content

AI Content continued to support Star Citizen’s monthly release cadence.

“It was exciting to see the comms calls start to make their way into the game as well as finally unveiling the NewsFlash content around the landing zones. These little updates will help provide players updates about the events happening around the ’verse.” AI Content Team

As they continued to develop these features, the devs requested additional functionality to allow for new features, such as scheduling, as well as scope-out work to make things like channels.

AI Content also continued to support the Mission teams as they integrated new comms content alongside new lines for Wikelo.

On larger-scale initiatives, the team worked alongside Combat AI to devise a new collection of wildline triggers for combatants and how they could (or whether they should) plug into the proposed line set for generic population NPCs.

The team also reviewed and standardized the trigger list used by behaviors across the game to ensure that there’s a single list of context words that everyone is operating with. This will prevent confusion when building behaviors or structuring missions.

AI (Features)

In May, AI Features ensured Human combat is in an optimal state in several key areas: ammo management and behavior, cover usage, first reactions and perception, attack and defend areas, investigations, grenade use, tactics, and medical behavior. The main focus is to stabilize and reach ‘gold standard’ for each.

In pursuit of the above, various issues were fixed, including NPCs looting ammo too close to hostiles, NPCs handling light switch disruption, and first reactions triggering simultaneously and putting the AI into an unresponsive state. A bug was also fixed that caused NPCs to incorrectly count ammo and evaluate remaining resources, causing them to loot more than necessary.

Various improvements were made too, including how NPCs select and use cover for shooting. They also made it easier to add new information to the AIWeaponComponent debug, and improved the ‘investigate’ flow to work better over a range of conditions with multiple NPCs at different awareness levels.

The devs also customized the friendly-fire check so that it can be balanced to give NPCs the desired behavior and prevent them from shooting when players feel they shouldn’t.

The wildlines setup channel was updated to enable the devs to mute and suppress already queued lines after the death of an NPC.

Defend-area and combat-movement queries were also updated to ensure NPCs don’t get stuck in spawn closets. For example, if too many NPCs are set to enter a 3m x 6m area, they will get stuck.

New tech and features were implemented too, including logic to prevent low-to-medium priority wildlines from triggering during TrackView sequences that NPCs are involved in.

Logic was also added for switching the aim target location to the visible element of the body while considering aiming priority (torso then head).

AI Features also finished work to ensure NPCs animatedly react to compromised cover, cleaned up the NPC-medic flow to make it more robust and improve the visuals, added additional debugging to balance first reaction times for audio and visual events, and added ‘trait debugging’ to prevent conflicting behavior traits.

A fix was added for placed dead bodies to prevent them from causing the AI to react when, from a story perspective, they already exist in the world.

Finally for AI Features, the team added audio proc clips to takedown animations so that nearby AI are alerted. They also added debug logging to disturbance events to prevent AI from reacting before the level has started properly.

AI (Game Intelligence Development Team)

In May, the Game Intelligence Development team began work on the UI prototype for Mission System v2; specifically the ‘outline header’ design, including the mission object properties design, the outline infrastructure, and a generic outline panel. This also involved creating UI visuals for the outline with all its components.

Alongside this, the team also fixed small bugs and worked on features requested by the game designers to improve StarScript.

AI (Tech)

Last month, AI Tech continued to improve how navigation links connect to external zones. The team are currently updating links that utilize motion warp, such as mantle or jumping down, to rely on specific metrics, which will enable them to be utilized by different categories of creatures. Updates were also made to the chase movement request to allow multiple destinations around bigger targets, like ground vehicles or apex creatures.

The first stage of ongoing improvements to 3D navigation was completed. This involved voxelizing custom areas and allowing them to define granularity. Currently, the voxelization data is being used to improve collision avoidance during AI ship flight.

The core work for serializing Subsumption variables was completed, which is used for network synchronization and the save-and-load mechanism.

For the Subsumption conversation feature, a clustering algorithm was added to split participants into more meaningful groups. This group data will be used to create avoidance obstacles, meaning NPCs will be able to avoid others already in a conversation group.

On the tools side, multiple usability improvements were made to StarScript, such as allowing bulk node deletion and the discarding of invalid sub-platforms when loading a platform or marking a document as modified when re-ordering variables.

Animation

The Facial Animation team recorded and processed content for upcoming releases for both new and existing mission givers, including Wikelo. They also continued to provide new voice packs that will populate generic NPCs throughout the ‘verse and began supporting the recently added NewsFlash content. Animations were developed for an upcoming creature, too.

Art (Characters)

May saw the Character Art team progress with new creatures, a heavy armor, and gameplay rewards. They also kicked off a light armor.

The Concept Art team prepared handoff sheets and explored future in-game armor rewards.

Art (Ships)

As usual, May was extremely busy for the Vehicle Content teams as they supported new releases, progressed with upcoming vehicles, and kicked off projects for the next year or so.

In Europe, four unannounced ships progressed. The first officially entered production, while the second progressed toward its upcoming whitebox review gate. The third continued down the production pipeline, with the artists currently awaiting feedback from the LOD0 review. The fourth received considerable attention during its whitebox phase, particularly around the cockpit entry requirements, as it will receive entirely new enter and exit animations (something rarely done to this level).

For already announced ships, the Anvil Paladin progressed through greybox, benefiting from the recent work on the Asgard to help speed up its creation.

The Consolidated Outland Pioneer continued its long and extensive whitebox phase.

“The sheer scale and complexity of this ship mean this is a longer-than-normal phase!” Vehicle Content Team

Then, after a short pause to help close out the Invictus ships, work resumed on the Ironclad, with a focus on blocking out every room with the appropriate Drake kits.

With the Guardian MX live, the North American teams moved onto closing out an upcoming variant for its impending release, with the ship successfully passing its final review. Another unannounced vehicle passed its whitebox review following minor adjustments to one of its key mechanics.

The RSI Apollo Medivac and Triage passed their greybox reviews, with a focus on ensuring each med-bed module tier is distinct without being disruptively different to use. The RSI Perseus continued through greybox ready for its gate review early this month.

Community

The Community team spent much of May breaking down Community feedback/sentiment across all platforms and ensuring its delivery to the right teams internally. The team published the Save the Date announcement for Invictus Launch Week 2955, as well as providing Spectrum support with an informative guide and FAQ. They also advised the community of the new opportunity for Idris owners to name their ship, and made players aware of the changes introduced with Alpha 4.1.1.

Support for Invictus and the accompanying Free Fly also included multiple Comm-Links, such as the manufacturer schedule, a referral bonus promotion, and Q&As for the Greycat MTC, Mirai Guardian MX and Anvil Asgard. The team also supported a social media selfie screenshot contest, which allowed players to show off their best looks at a variety of exotic locales around the ‘verse.

Throughout May, the team connected with the community as part of the 2025 Bar Citizen World Tour. This included venues in the United States, Korea, China, Spain, Germany, and France. The team published an invitation to the upcoming International Bar Citizen Weekend 2025, and have plans to visit additional locations throughout the year. Correspondingly, submissions were announced for CitizenCon Direct Watch Parties that will pair the camaraderie of Bar Citizen with the energy of CitizenCon! The team is currently deep in planning for this year's event, which is shaping up to be a fun one!

Finally, alongside evergreen tasks such as This Week in Star Citizen, the bi-weekly Roadmap Updates and Roundups, Monthly Reports (like this one!) and the monthly refresh of the Arena Commander Schedule, the Community team supported the epic conclusion to the System 7 race series presented by ATMO esports.

Core Gameplay

Core Gameplay are currently working through a long list of weapon improvements to further modernize the FPS experience for both Squadron 42 and Star Citizen, including tweaking how disruptive weapon raising is to the flow of combat. Engineering and Design collaborated to iterate on these improvements and provide more polished combat gameplay.

Work on hacking continued, which involved highlighting suggested abilities for certain gameplay situations. Abilities are also now disabled when they’re not applicable in a specific situation to better explain hacking gameplay. The hacking terminal now also supports color-coded terminal output for better clarity.

The team also wrapped up work on the new Argo ATLS IKTI and GEO IKTI, both of which support weapons instead of their utility attachments. Additional bug fixes and polish are underway, but the team is excited to further expand the ATLS platform and provide players with more options on the battlefield.

For Engineering, the team reviewed feedback and outstanding work before dividing the feature into smaller milestones. The first milestone primarily covers core gameplay mechanics, such as the engineering screen and its ability to manipulate power distribution and item states. A recent internal review provided feedback and polish that will be addressed before the feature reaches players. The diagnostics screen also received new functionality and utility.

As part of the ongoing quality-of-life initiative, Core Gameplay are working on improvements to the harvestable and loot systems. This is to address various performance issues and, more importantly, give the designers more control over how harvestables and loot are spawned.

For Alpha 4.1.1 the devs enabled the ability for players to quantum travel to their own vehicles, which was received positively by the community.

Item Recovery is currently progressing, with tasks for tier 1 progressing.

As part of the space combat-focused content in Alpha 4.1.1, Core Gameplay supported Design in tweaking and tuning recoil for vehicle weapons. In collaboration with SFX, VFX, and Vehicle Content, they made a concerted push to polish the combat experience in cockpits and turrets and are hoping to expand this to more weapons soon.

As an additional stepping stone toward the new vehicle radar and scanning system, changes were made to the information available to players before a ship is scanned. The team are currently reviewing the feedback that came from this change and are looking to implement improvements that smooth out that flow.

Quantum interdiction is also being reworked to be more compatible with Server Meshing, leveraging tech developed for Alpha 4.1 to communicate across different volumes on different servers. This rework is primarily about reliability, not the mechanic itself.

“We recognize that there’s an imbalance between lawful and unlawful gameplay and want to ensure players on both ends have the tools needed to contend with the other.” Core Gameplay Team

The recent work on control surfaces reached a major milestone, with most of the atmospheric flight model behaviors now in first-pass implementation. As part of this, ships will now more accurately reflect the expected flight behavior based on lift, drag, angle of attack, and other factors. Thrusters currently activate smoothly to compensate for different atmospheric densities, while hovering feels more natural.

The Core Gameplay team fixed numerous issues related to cargo crates intersecting with each other alongside the ability to retrieve multiple vehicles from a hangar. Players now also receive a warning when their ship accumulates distortion damage.

For upcoming gameplay, medical beds now heal radiation damage. A pass was also done to ensure players receive proper visual feedback on radiation in the environment.

The transit rework (internally referred to as the ‘transport system’) continued toward the first playable version for internal validation. The team moved transport from ‘push system’ to ‘serialized variables’ on the Transport Manager for improved reliability. To validate the new system, Design trialed the transport system in the New Babbage habs. They’re currently addressing feedback and issues resulting from the test.

For the Apex Valakkar, Core Gameplay supported the Character and AI teams on multiple fronts. For example, the irradiated Apex Valakkar’s projectiles will now spawn hazard volumes that damage the player over time. The apex creature also spawns a “mole hill” wherever it exits or enters the ground.

FPS radar and scanning also progressed. The devs can now specify if contacts should remain visible for extended periods after they have been first scanned, which is useful to the designers in curated situations. Additionally, they can now reduce the signature of a contact if it’s considered dead. For example, dead NPCs are no longer detectable from the same distances as living ones.

As part of the upcoming patch release, a lot of feedback was received around the reliability and quality of the new comms notifications. As a result, the team is working through various improvements to ensure mission givers appear at their best and don’t awkwardly look at players.

Finally for Core Gameplay, the team are currently supporting an upcoming Global Event, including new ways to track and display player progress.

Lighting

Lighting supported all recent and upcoming patch releases, including adding environmental and dynamic lighting to interactable event locations in Pyro.

Locations

The Locations teams continued to support the ongoing monthly content releases. Last month, there was a particular focus on Invictus Launch Week, with the devs looking forward to releases in July and August alongside updates to Wikelo.

Narrative

May brought with it a flurry of activity for the Narrative team. The top of the month saw them tackling bugs found in Alpha 4.1.1 PTU in preparation for the patch’s full release. Simultaneously, members of the team finalized new content that will be heavily narrative focused and even feature audio recordings for players to discover.

Beyond that, dozens of new mission contracts were created for upcoming gameplay to not only provide players with critical information but a sense of character as well. The writers also worked on scripts for new mission providers who will be making an appearance later this year.

“Because of the time involved with writing, recording, and processing performances, there’s an interesting balance of locking down a script while allowing for the Design team to continue refining the gameplay as they continue development. This often means that we record alternate lines that would be useful in case the scope or design of a new mission needs to be adjusted closer to release.” Narrative Team

Finally, the team solidified the story plans for next year, taking the initial high-level outline and pulling in more details to help other teams continue with their planning.

Online Technology

In May, the Network team continued work on Dynamic Server Meshing, separating the DGS assignment from the territory manager. The objective is to base territory runtime redistribution on several factors, including entity and player distribution and overall shard occupancy. Subsequent work will remove territories from the equation altogether, allowing compute resources to be deployed exactly where they're needed.

The Live Tools team worked on improving moderation tools to provide a better user experience for everyone. They also improved the solution that allows the Publishing team to schedule in-game messages and continued to add smaller improvements to the various tools used across development. New infrastructure was deployed to better handle game crashes and errors too.

Online Services continued work on the Item Imprint system, including the design aspects, and progressed with diffusion removal to lay the groundwork for the social refactor. Online Services also continued to help fix various issues that were discovered by players alongside minor improvements to the mission-system tools.

UI

In May, the team completed the UI for an upcoming event, creating various screens to support the narrative and gameplay. Once completed, the Design teams kicked off plans for the next one.

The new Mirai UI was also finished, which the team kept quiet until the launch of the Guardian MX.

“Mirai uses vibrant colors and dynamic shapes, which were great fun to work on and mark an interesting departure from the retro sci-fi look of our other styles, like Drake and Aegis.” UI Team

The new layout and shapes were a challenge to implement with the existing setup. So, the team assessed the problems and rewrote the UI core to make it easier to create more interesting styles in the future.

Elsewhere, performance improvements continued, with the team investigating spreading UI processing across multiple cores. Visual prototypes were also worked on for some interesting but currently confidential 3D interactive UIs to replace one of the older systems in the game.

title: This Week in Star Citizen
summary: 06/02/2025 - 2:00 PM This Week in Star Citizen Happy Monday, everyone!
body_html:
06/02/2025 - 2:00 PM This Week in Star Citizen Happy Monday, everyone!

Alpha 4.2 is now available to all waves in the PTU! If you haven’t checked it out, now’s a great time to jump in and help us kick the tires of the latest build - your feedback goes a long way toward smoothing out the rough edges before its Live release. A huge thanks to everyone who’s already hopped in and shared their thoughts; we appreciate it, and keep it coming!

Throughout the month of June, we’re celebrating YOU, our vibrant and inclusive community, and we want to see your flair on display! Whether you’re designing something eye-catching, baking tasty treats, customizing your fleet, or flying proudly in your favorite livery, this is your moment to shine. Submit your most colorful creations for the Show Us Your Colors Celebration 2025 and you could walk away with some sweet rewards!

This past Saturday, we had the pleasure of attending Bar Citizen Lyon, an incredible gathering organized by Star Citizen Francophone, Himalia, and Pulsar 42. Around 300 Citizens showed up, including the next generation of UEE recruits and a few adorable pet kopions. From the quiz machine and org showcases to giveaways and hours of passionate conversation, Ninkasi La Guillotière was buzzing with energy!

Next up: Bar Citizen Toronto kicks off on June 7, followed by International Bar Citizen Weekend events happening worldwide near all our studios on June 14 -15. We’re putting the finishing touches on our plans and look forward to seeing you there! For all the details on times and locations, check out the World Tour Comm-Link.

Now, let's see what's going on this week

This Tuesday, as we lead up to the release of Alpha 4.2, we’ll be dropping a new Patch Watch, showcasing upcoming features, improvements, and fixes that aren’t listed on the Public Roadmap. Plus, keep an eye out for the June Subscriber Comm-Link and the latest Subscriber Newsletter.

Wednesday brings the latest Roadmap Update, accompanied by its complementary Roadmap Roundup. You can also look forward to the May 2025 PU Monthly Report for a behind-the-scenes look at what the dev teams were working on throughout the month.

Thursday's episode of Inside Star Citizen takes a look at the new sandbox activity unfolding in the next chapter of the ongoing Regen Crisis narrative.

Friday, you'll find a copy of the weekly RSI Newsletter delivered straight to your inbox.

On Saturday, the Bar Citizen World Tour touches down in Toronto, Canada - more details here.

Fly low, and fly fast!
